vulnerabilities.description: openSIS 5.1 before 9.0 contains a local file inclusion vulnerability that allows authenticated users to include arbitrary files through the modname parameter of ajax.php. Attackers can prefix a payload with misc/ and use ../ directory traversal to read sensitive files like /etc/passwd or execute local scripts in the web server context. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-19.

GNOME gnome-keyring 3.4.0 through 3.4.1, when gpg-cache-method is set to "idle" or "timeout," does not properly limit the amount of time a passphrase is cached, which allows attackers to have an unspecified impact via unknown attack vectors.

GNOME Keyring through 3.28.2 allows local users to retrieve login credentials via a Secret Service API call and the D-Bus interface if the keyring is unlocked, a similar issue to CVE-2008-7320. One perspective is that this occurs because available D-Bus protection mechanisms (involving the busconfig and policy XML elements) are not used. NOTE: the vendor disputes this because, according to the security model, untrusted applications must not be allowed to access the user's session bus socket.

Baidu UEditor 1.4.0 through 1.4.3.3 contains an unrestricted file upload vulnerability in the catchimage action of /ueditor/net/controller.ashx that only validates the Content-Type header. Unauthenticated attackers can supply a source[] URL like x.jpg?.aspx to retain a malicious extension and write an executable .aspx file for remote code execution. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-17.

FineReport 8.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary files through the resourcepath parameter of the /WebReport/ReportServer endpoint. Attackers can send GET requests with op=chart and cmd=get_geo_json to read sensitive files like privilege.xml and extract admin credentials. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-19.

A flaw was found in all released versions of m2crypto, where they are vulnerable to Bleichenbacher timing attacks in the RSA decryption API via the timed processing of valid PKCS#1 v1.5 Ciphertext. The highest threat from this vulnerability is to confidentiality.

Rocket.Chat versions 0.61.0 before 3.11.4, 3.12.x before 3.12.4 and 3.13.x before 3.13.2 contain a missing authorization vulnerability allowing unauthenticated attackers to read any room's messages via the livechat:loadHistory Meteor method. Attackers can mint a guest token through livechat:registerGuest and send POST requests to /api/v1/method.callAnon with a target rid parameter to retrieve message history without membership checks. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2025-02-13.

OTOBO 10.0.1 before 10.0.13 contains an open redirect vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to redirect users by supplying arbitrary URLs to the ExternalURLJump action. Attackers can craft GET requests to /otobo/index.pl?Action=ExternalURLJump with a malicious URL parameter, which the ExternalURLJump.pm module redirects to without an allow-list check, enabling phishing attacks. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-23.

Synway SMG Gateway Management Software builds through 2022-03-15 contain a path traversal vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary files via the downfile parameter in /down.php. Attackers can send a multipart POST request to /down.php with a traversal path in downfile to retrieve sensitive files like /etc/passwd. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-20.

JoomBri Careers 3.3.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts through the 'keyword' parameter of the /for-jobseekers/search-jobs endpoint in com_jbcareers. Attackers can craft malicious URLs using an attribute-breakout payload with onfocus and autofocus to execute arbitrary JavaScript and steal session tokens or credentials. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2023-10-23.
SQUID is vulnerable to HTTP request smuggling, caused by chunked decoder lenience, allows a remote attacker to perform Request/Response smuggling past firewall and frontend security systems.

OpenMage magento-lts before 20.2.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability because the TinyMCE WYSIWYG editor fails to filter scripts in specially crafted HTML tags. Attackers can inject an img element with a malicious onmouseover attribute to execute scripts in the browsers of users viewing the rendered content.

httparty before 0.21.0 is vulnerable to an assumed-immutable web parameter vulnerability. A remote and unauthenticated attacker can provide a crafted filename parameter during multipart/form-data uploads which could result in attacker controlled filenames being written.

Bagisto 2.1.0 before 2.2.1 contains a client-side template injection vulnerability in the search page where the 'query' parameter is rendered unescaped inside a Vue app root. Unauthenticated attackers can send crafted VueJS template expressions to the /bagisto-common/search endpoint via the 'query' parameter to execute arbitrary JavaScript in victims' browsers. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2024-07-30.

Flowise v3.0.1 < 3.0.8, and 3.0.8 < 3.1.3 with 'ALLOW_BUILTIN_DEP' enabled contain an authenticated remote code execution vulnerability and node VM sandbox escape due to insecure use of integrated modules (Puppeteer and Playwright) within the nodevm execution environment. An authenticated attacker able to create or run a tool that leverages Puppeteer/Playwright can specify attacker-controlled browser binary paths and parameters. When the tool executes, the attacker-controlled executable/parameters are run on the host and circumvent the intended nodevm sandbox restrictions, resulting in execution of arbitrary code in the context of the host. This vulnerability was incorrectly assigned as a duplicate CVE-2025-26319 by the developers and should be considered distinct from that identifier.

Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal') vulnerability in Erlang OTP (stdlib modules) allows Absolute Path Traversal, File Manipulation.

This vulnerability is associated with program files lib/stdlib/src/zip.erl and program routines zip:unzip/1, zip:unzip/2, zip:extract/1, zip:extract/2 unless the memory option is passed.

This issue affects OTP from OTP 17.0 before OTP 26.2.5.13, OTP 27.3.4.1, and OTP 28.0.1, corresponding to stdlib from 2.0 before 5.2.3.4, 6.2.2.1, and 7.0.1.

An use of hard-coded cryptographic key vulnerability has been reported to affect Hybrid Backup Sync. If exploited, the vulnerability could allow remote attackers to compromise the security of the system.

We have already fixed the vulnerability in the following version:
Hybrid Backup Sync 26.4.0.521 and later
Hybrid Backup Sync 26.4.1.563 and later

Zipline before 4.0.2 contains a predictable filename vulnerability that allows attackers to infer other users' upload filenames by recovering the Math.random generator state. Attackers with five consecutive gfycat-style filenames can reconstruct the random state to predict previous and future filenames until the instance restarts, exposing private uploads.

lwext4 through 1.0.0 contains a heap buffer overflow in ext4_fs_init_inode_bitmap() in src/ext4_fs.c because it does not validate s_inodes_per_group against the inode bitmap size. Attackers can supply a crafted ext4 image with an oversized s_inodes_per_group so memset writes past the heap buffer, corrupting memory and crashing the mounting application.

lwext4 through 1.0.0 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in ext4_fs_init_block_bitmap() that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory via crafted superblock geometry fields. Attackers can supply an ext4 image with oversized s_reserved_gdt_blocks and BLOCK_UNINIT groups to write past the bitmap buffer, crashing applications that mount it.

A container privilege escalation flaw was found in certain Multi-Cloud Object Gateway Core images. This issue stems from the /etc/passwd file being created with group-writable permissions during build time. In certain conditions, an attacker who can execute commands within an affected container, even as a non-root user, can leverage their membership in the root group to modify the /etc/passwd file. This could allow the attacker to add a new user with any arbitrary UID, including UID 0, leading to full root privileges within the container

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

xen-netback: Fix UAF when reading statistics data

The network statistic data in the driver is protected by RCU.
Unfortunately when tearing down the queues after an error during
connecting to the frontend (e.g. due to illegal Xenstore data filled
in by the guest), the statistic data is being freed without
synchronizing the RCU state.  In case the data is being read via sysfs
in this phase, access to already freed memory or memory being in new
use is possible.

Fix that by calling synchronize_net() before freeing the queue data.

This is XSA-526 / CVE-2026-100080

Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data vulnerability in WP Swings PDF Generator for WordPress pdf-generator-for-wp allows Retrieve Embedded Sensitive Data.This issue affects PDF Generator for WordPress: from n/a through 1.6.5.

Contrast before 1.21.0 contains a panic vulnerability in the transit-engine endpoint's ciphertextContainer.UnmarshalJSON function that fails to validate decoded ciphertext length before slicing. An authenticated workload with a valid mesh certificate can trigger a runtime panic by submitting a short base64-encoded ciphertext, causing log spam and request failures without crashing the process.

Contrast (Edgeless Systems) before 1.21.0 performs unanchored suffix matching when selecting per-registry configuration in the imagepuller. Config.registryFor strips a single trailing dot and then uses strings.HasSuffix(hostname, fqdn) without requiring a DNS label boundary, so a registry entry such as [registries."ghcr.io."] is also applied to any host whose name merely ends in that byte sequence, including attacker-registered domains such as evilghcr.io. When an image or layer is pulled from such a sibling domain, the imagepuller sends the configured Authorization header (basic auth, registry token, or identity token), trusts the configured custom CA bundle, follows the configured mirror, and honours insecure-skip-verify (disabling TLS verification) for that host. Image integrity is not affected, as image bytes remain pinned by digest in the policy and are validated after the pull. Configurations that use a leading dot (e.g., [registries.".example.registry"]) are unaffected.

Penpot before 2.18.0 binds the MCP server plugin WebSocket bridge to all network interfaces without authentication in single-user mode. Unauthenticated attackers on adjacent networks can connect to the WebSocket port to impersonate the Penpot browser plugin, intercept task payloads, and return forged results to the MCP client.

An OS command Injection issue exists in Air Terminal 6 provided by SoftBank Corp. Arbitrary commands may be executed with the root privilege by a user who can connect to the affected product via a wired or Wi-Fi connection.

Vulnerability in the Oracle Communications Unified Inventory Management product of Oracle Communications (component: Security).  Supported versions that are affected are 7.5.0, 7.5.1, 7.6.0, 7.7.0, 7.8.0 and 8.0.1. Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in takeover of Oracle Communications Unified Inventory Management. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 7.5 (Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H).

Vulnerability in the MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster product of Oracle MySQL (component: InnoDB).  Supported versions that are affected are MySQL Server: 8.4.0-8.4.12, 9.7.0-9.7.3, 26.7.0-26.7.1; MySQL Cluster: 8.0.0-8.0.49, 8.4.0-8.4.12, 9.7.0-9.7.3 and  26.7.0-26.7.1. Difficult to exploit vulnerability allows high privileged attacker with logon to the infrastructure where MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster executes to compromise MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster.  Successful attacks require human interaction from a person other than the attacker. Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in unauthorized ability to cause a hang or frequently repeatable crash (complete DOS) of MySQL Server, MySQL Cluster. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 4.0 (Availability impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:H/UI:R/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H).

OpenClaw Windows Node through 2026.11.3 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the canvas.present capability that bypasses URL risk evaluation enforced by canvas.navigate. Attackers with gateway or agent access can issue canvas.present to make the node's WebView send requests to localhost, private networks, or tailnet services from the user's machine.

An uncontrolled recursion vulnerability exists in the LINE iOS app prior to version 26.19.0.

The Flex Message processing component does not adequately validate the structure of externally supplied message content.

As a result, an attacker who is able to send a crafted message to a victim could cause the application to crash when the message is received or displayed.

A server-side mitigation has been deployed that also protects existing iOS clients that have not been updated to version 26.19.0.

A SQL injection vulnerability when the recipient tapped on a specially crafted “order details” message from an unofficial client in WhatsApp for Android prior to version 2.26.35.74 could have allowed deletion of locally-stored WhatsApp files and, only if the user is online at time of receipt, leaked one bit of information asked by the attacker about the user’s chat database via an induced-crash delivery receipt timing sidechannel. We have not seen evidence of exploitation in the wild.

Connaisseur is an admission controller that integrates container image signature verification into a Kubernetes cluster. Prior to 3.11.1, the Cosign validator counts valid signature layers rather than distinct trust roots for trustRoot: "*" policies using an explicit threshold or an implicit require-all policy. An attacker who controls one configured trust root's signing key and can attach multiple signatures to an image can satisfy a threshold intended to require multiple independent roots, causing admission without the intended signer quorum. Policies using a single trust root or the required option are not affected. This issue is fixed in 3.11.1.

virtualenv is a tool for creating isolated virtual python environments. Prior to 21.7.12, download_wheel() accepts pip and setuptools seed wheels fetched for periodic updates or the --download option without checking their bytes against an authoritative digest equivalent to the embedded wheels' BUNDLE_SHA256 verification. A compromised index, stale mirror, or intercepted TLS connection can substitute a different wheel under the requested distribution, version, and filename, after which virtualenv caches and seeds the attacker-controlled wheel into subsequently created environments. The verification applies to the default PyPI path and is intentionally skipped when PIP_INDEX_URL, PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL, or PIP_INDEX configures a custom index that may legitimately publish rebuilt wheels. This issue is fixed in version 21.7.12.

virtualenv is a tool for creating isolated virtual python environments. Prior to 21.7.12, BatchActivator.quote() returns prompt text unchanged before activate.bat inserts it into a cmd.exe set "VAR=value" statement. An attacker who influences --prompt, VIRTUALENV_PROMPT, or the corresponding configuration value can include a double quote that closes the assignment and leaves following cmd.exe operators as executable syntax. When a user activates the generated Windows environment, the injected commands run with that user's privileges. This issue is fixed in version 21.7.12.

virtualenv is a tool for creating isolated virtual python environments. Prior to 21.7.11, PyEnvCfg.write() writes prompt values verbatim to the line-oriented pyvenv.cfg format while PyEnvCfg._read_values() parses the file with str.splitlines() and accepts the last value for duplicate keys. An attacker who influences --prompt, VIRTUALENV_PROMPT, or configuration input can insert a recognized line boundary and additional keys, including home, causing consumers to use an attacker-selected base interpreter or corrupted environment metadata. The security impact requires prompt input from outside the operator's trust boundary; directly supplied prompt content primarily corrupts the operator's own environment. This issue is fixed in version 21.7.11.

bep/imagemeta is a Go library for reading EXIF, IPTC and XMP image meta data from JPEG, TIFF, PNG, and WebP files. Prior to 0.17.3, imagemeta.Decode could exhaust memory when parsing PNG zTXt chunks whose keyword is "Raw profile type iptc": the declared chunk length can drive an allocation far larger than the input file, and the embedded zlib stream is decompressed without an output limit. The advisory reports a 42-byte input causing a 256 MB allocation and a 127 KB input inflating to 460 MB. The oversized-allocation path's memory effect depends on platform overcommit and configured GOMEMLIMIT or cgroup limits, while the decompression path reliably creates resident memory. Applications that decode untrusted PNGs with IPTC metadata processing can therefore suffer denial of service through memory exhaustion. This issue is fixed in 0.17.3.

Paymenter is a free and open-source webshop solution for management of hosting services. Prior to 1.5.7, the HasConfirmation trait in app/Livewire/Traits/HasConfirmation.php, included by app/Livewire/Component.php across 36 client-facing Livewire components, exposed executeConfirmedAction as a public action that invoked any component method accepted by method_exists. The action could call inherited InteractsWithProperties::fill(), whose data_set() writes arbitrary public properties, including state marked with #[Locked] and dotted paths into hydrated Eloquent models. Depending on the methods and properties exposed by an individual component, an unauthenticated caller could use this path to bypass intended authorization and modify server-side state intended to be immutable or protected from client-side manipulation. This issue is fixed in version 1.5.7.

ALTCHA is a Go library for creating and verifying ALTCHA challenges. Prior to 2.1.0, parseServerSignature can leave ServerSignatureVerificationData.Extra uninitialized when url.ParseQuery returns partial values and an error for a malformed percent escape in VerificationData. A later write of an unknown parsed key to the nil map panics before VerifyServerSignature or VerifyServerSignatureSafe completes signature verification, so an unauthenticated client can abort a request. Standard net/http recovers the request goroutine, while application goroutines or frameworks without recovery can crash the process. This issue is fixed in version 2.1.0.

TeamPass is a self-hosted collaborative password manager. Prior to 3.2.1.2, the update_folder action in app/sources/folders.queries.php allowed an authenticated, non-read-only user to re-parent a folder without checking whether the target folder or submitted parentId belonged to the caller's user-accessible_folders set. Selecting a personal folder as the new parent passed the personal-folder guard and set personal_folder on the target, transferring the credential subtree into the attacker's accessible space after the next login and hiding it from the organization, including administrators. The change exposed credential labels, logins, URLs, email addresses, and descriptions, while sharekey-protected passwords remained protected; hiding the subtree also denied other users access. This issue is fixed in version 3.2.1.2.

Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal') vulnerability in gleam-lang gleam allows a malicious package publisher to delete a directory outside the project's build directory when a developer builds a project.

A Hex package release's metadata carries an app field with the release's OTP application name. Gleam reads this field from the hex.pm release API when it downloads dependencies and uses it as the package's build directory name without validating it (hex_manifest_package in compiler-cli/src/dependencies.rs, ProjectPaths::build_directory_for_package). When a dependency fails to compile, Gleam deletes that directory with remove_dir_all. hex.pm didn't restrict the field to a directory name before 2026-10-12, so a publisher could set it to a value such as ../../../../target or an absolute path. When a project depends on such a release directly or transitively and the release fails to compile, gleam build, gleam check, gleam run, gleam test or gleam export deletes the directory the name resolves to. For a pure Gleam package no publisher code runs.

This issue affects gleam: from 0.32.4 before 1.19.2.

A CRLF injection vulnerability in WatchGuard Dimension's outgoing email server configuration allows an authenticated Dimension Administrator to execute arbitrary operating system commands on the Dimension appliance with the privileges of the local mail-handling account.

An OS command injection vulnerability in WatchGuard Dimension's package update functionality allows an authenticated Dimension Administrator to execute arbitrary operating system commands as root by submitting a specially crafted package update request.

Fabio is an HTTP(S) and TCP router for deploying applications managed by consul. Prior to 1.7.3, route/table.go selects targets using raw req.URL.Path, while proxy/http_proxy.go applies per-route ACL and basic-auth checks to the selected target and forwards the raw path to the origin. Dot-segment, encoded-dot, or repeated-slash variants can fall through to a less restrictive route that reaches the same backend; the backend then normalizes the path and serves the protected resource without the configured access controls. A less restrictive fallback route must reach the same backend; without one, the request returns 404. This issue is fixed in version 1.7.3.

pREST (PostgreSQL REST) is an API that delivers an application on top of a Postgres database. Prior to 2.4.0, the vulnerable parameter is _groupby, handled by GroupByClause in adapters/postgres/postgres.go. adapters/postgres/postgres.go uses the weaker isSafeSQLExpression check for this function-expression branch instead of the stricter single-field validator used for _select. That check validates only the outer function name against a 13-function allowlist and permits nested subqueries, trailing UNION syntax, and inner pg_ functions. controllers/crud.go concatenates the GROUP BY expression while parameterizing only WHERE values, allowing attacker-controlled SQL structure into the clause. Default configuration permits unauthenticated access; a restricted installation may require a low-privilege table reader. UNION-based extraction requires compatible column counts and types and was not verified end to end, but a delay-producing function can cause denial of service without that alignment. This issue is fixed in 2.4.0.

LinkAce is a self-hosted archive to collect website links. Prior to 2.6.0, LinkController::update() in app/Http/Controllers/API/LinkController.php passes $request->all() to the repository update method even though user_id is fillable and is not an allowed field in the validated update request. An authenticated API user who is authorized to update a link can therefore assign an arbitrary or nonexistent user_id, transferring the link into another user's bookmark collection or orphaning it from any real account. The web update controller is unaffected because it passes only validated fields. This issue is fixed in version 2.6.0.

LinkAce is a self-hosted archive to collect website links. Prior to 2.6.0, the authenticated GET /lists/{list}/feed and GET /tags/{tag}/feed handlers in app/Http/Controllers/App/FeedController.php use integer route model binding without an object-level authorization or visibility check. Unlike the web list controller, which invokes LinkListPolicy::view(), the feed controller lets a normal authenticated user enumerate another user's private list or tag and receive its name and feed metadata, along with public or internal bookmark entries associated with that taxonomy. The existing per-link visibility filter still excludes PRIVATE link records, so the disclosure is limited to the private taxonomy and its non-private member links. This issue is fixed in version 2.6.0.

aMQTT is an open source MQTT broker and client. From 0.11.0 until 0.11.4, add_subscription() in amqtt/broker.py accepts malformed single-level + wildcard placement because it checks substrings instead of validating each slash-delimited level. The _matches() function converts each + into a greedy regular-expression fragment and evaluates it with re.fullmatch(), allowing a filter containing many adjacent + characters to trigger catastrophic backtracking when compared with a topic that partially matches but ultimately fails. Because matching runs synchronously in _run_broadcast(), one subscription followed by a publish can block the broker event loop, stopping message delivery and new connection processing until restart. Anonymous clients can trigger the issue with the default configuration. Any authenticated client permitted to create arbitrary subscriptions and publish messages may still exploit it when authentication is enabled. This issue is fixed in version 0.11.4.

A flaw was found in libtirpc. The SunRPC UDP/datagram server transport reuses a single receive buffer across requests and resets the XDR decode position without rebinding the decode length to the size of the datagram actually received. As a result, when a short UDP RPC request is received after a longer one, the XDR decoder can read stale bytes left in the reused buffer and interpret them as part of the current request, including credential, verifier, or procedure-argument fields. The highest threat from this vulnerability is to data confidentiality and integrity for services that use a UDP-based SunRPC server.

A flaw was found in cifs-utils. This flaw allows an unprivileged local user to achieve privilege escalation. When a privileged service mounts a Common Internet File System (CIFS) share using a user-controlled credentials file, input values are not properly sanitized before being assembled into mount options. A local attacker can exploit this vulnerability to inject unauthorized mount options, allowing them to bypass permission checks and execute files with administrative (root) privileges.

CKAN is an open-source data management system for data hubs and data portals. Prior to 2.10.11 and 2.11.6, the web user registration flow authenticates a newly registered account without first regenerating the session identifier when server-side session storage is configured. An attacker who can set a session cookie in a victim's browser or obtain the victim's current valid session identifier can reuse that identifier after the victim registers, gaining access to the new account. CKAN uses cookie-based sessions by default, and web registration is disabled by default through ckan.auth.create_user_via_web. This issue is fixed in CKAN 2.10.11, 2.11.6, and 2.12.0.

Chevereto before 4.5.8 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to cause the server to issue arbitrary requests by supplying a malicious URL to the uploadToWebsite function, which fetches the raw source via fetch_url before the Upload::checkValidUrl SSRF guard can be invoked. Attackers can target loopback addresses, RFC1918 internal services, cloud instance metadata endpoints, and file/gopher/dict schemes through the /json upload action to disclose internal responses or credentials when the fetched content is stored and served back as a public image URL.

OpenRemote is an open-source internet-of-things platform. Prior to 1.31.0, an authenticated user who obtains another user's MQTT session ID can disconnect that session across realm boundaries through the GET route GET {realm}/disconnect/{sessionID}. In manager/src/main/java/org/openremote/manager/security/UserResourceImpl.java, disconnectUserSession ignores the requested realm and calls mqttBrokerService.disconnectSession(sessionID) without checking session ownership; model/src/main/java/org/openremote/model/security/UserResource.java exposes the route without an @RolesAllowed restriction. The earlier cross-realm read-method guards did not cover this disconnect method, and same-realm users can also disconnect sessions they do not own. Session IDs are not trivially brute-forceable but may be exposed through monitoring, logs, or correlated API calls, and the unauthorized disconnect can disrupt MQTT connectivity across tenant boundaries without directly disclosing session data. This issue is fixed in 1.31.0.

The King Addons for Elementor – 100+ Elementor Widgets, 4 000+ Elementor Templates, WooCommerce Builder, Mega Menu, Popup Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 51.1.89. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to read arbitrary post meta values — including private contact data, API keys, license keys, and plugin-internal metadata — for any published post by supplying an arbitrary meta key name via the unauthenticated AJAX endpoint. The nonce check present in the handler provides no effective barrier because the nonce is emitted into every front-end page for logged-out visitors via wp_localize_script.

Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) vulnerability in ShortPixel ShortPixel Image Optimizer shortpixel-image-optimiser allows Cross Site Request Forgery.This issue affects ShortPixel Image Optimizer: from n/a through 6.6.1.

Improper Certificate Validation vulnerability in the ssl application in Erlang/OTP allows a client that holds a certificate trusted by one SNI virtual host to authenticate to a second SNI virtual host on the same listener by resuming its TLS 1.2 session there.

A server that serves several SNI names from one listen socket through sni_fun or sni_hosts keeps one pre-TLS 1.3 session cache per listener and does not bind a cached session to the SNI name or client trust policy that established it. When an SNI option set switches to verify_peer without naming reuse_sessions, ssl_config:update_options/3 inherits the base listener's reuse_sessions value of true, so the default that disables reuse for client-authenticating servers does not apply. On an abbreviated handshake ssl_session:is_resumable/4 checks only that the cached session uses one of the current server certificates and carries some peer certificate, and never revalidates that certificate against the CA selected for the requested name. The names must share a server certificate, which is common with wildcard or multi-SAN certificates. TLS 1.3 does not use this cache and is not affected.

This issue affects OTP from OTP 18.0 before OTP 27.3.4.19, OTP 28.5.0.8, and OTP 29.1.2, corresponding to ssl from 7.0 before 11.2.12.14, 11.6.0.7, and 11.7.8.

Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in esaml_binding in dropbox esaml allows an unauthenticated attacker to exhaust the Erlang VM atom table and crash the node via a crafted SAMLResponse.

esaml_binding:decode_response/2 parses the decoded SAMLResponse with xmerl_scan:string/2, which interns every element name, attribute name, and namespace prefix it reads as a permanent atom. The SAML consume (ACS) and single-logout endpoints call it on unauthenticated requests before any signature check, so one well-formed document with thousands of distinct names mints thousands of atoms while staying inside the 128 KB request body limit. Atoms are never reclaimed and the VM caps the atom table at about one million entries, so a few dozen requests abort the node.

This issue affects esaml: from 0.1.0 onward.

Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification) vulnerability in hexpm hex_core allows an untrusted repository mirror, or a server answering hex_core's API requests, to exhaust the memory of the Erlang VM running hex_core. The same code is vendored in Hex (mix_hex_repo, mix_hex_api) and rebar3 (r3_hex_repo, r3_hex_api).

hex_repo:get_names/1, hex_repo:get_versions/1, hex_repo:get_package/2 and hex_repo:get_policy/2 decompress the registry response with zlib:gunzip/1 and decode the signed envelope before verifying its signature. A mirror doesn't have the repository's private key, but it chooses the compressed bytes, so a small response decompresses into an envelope of any size before the signature check rejects it.

hex_api decodes responses with the application/vnd.hex+erlang content type through hex_safe_binary_to_term:safe_binary_to_term/1, which calls binary_to_term(Binary, [safe]). The safe option prevents atom creation, but it accepts compressed terms and doesn't limit the size of the decoded term, and the check that rejects functions and ports runs after the term has been built. The fix for CVE-2026-21619 added the safe option and that check without bounding the decoded size.

This issue affects rebar3: from 3.9.1 before 3.27.3; hex: from 2.1.0 before 2.5.2 and from 2.6.0 onward; hex_core: from 0.1.0 before 0.20.0.

Improper Validation of Integrity Check Value vulnerability in hexpm hex allows a package mirror to substitute the tarball that mix hex.package fetch PACKAGE VERSION --output - writes to standard output.

Hex compares a fetched tarball's inner and outer checksums with the repository's signed registry before writing it to a file or unpacking it. The standard output branch of mix hex.package fetch writes the bytes returned by Hex.SCM.fetch/3 without that comparison, and Hex.SCM.fetch/3 doesn't verify freshly downloaded tarballs itself. When a mirror configured with HEX_MIRROR_URL or mirror_url serves altered bytes, the command prints them and exits successfully, while the same fetch with --output FILE fails with a checksum mismatch.

Hex also prints diagnostics to standard output while the command runs: the body of a failed HTTP response from the update check or a registry fetch, and API warnings from the x-hex-message header. A mirror that answers one of those requests with an error whose body is a tar archive gets that archive written to standard output ahead of the verified tarball, so a pipeline that unpacks standard output extracts the mirror's files. This happens even when the checksum check then fails, because the archive is already on standard output.

This issue affects hex: from 0.20.2 before 2.5.2.

Protection Mechanism Failure vulnerability in hexpm hex allows the owner of a package, or an attacker who has taken over the owner's account, to get a newly published release past the release-age cooldown.

The cooldown (cooldown config, HEX_COOLDOWN) withholds versions younger than the configured age during dependency resolution. When the release of a package locked in mix.lock is retired or has a security advisory, Hex.RemoteConverger.build_cooldown_bypass/3 and Hex.RemoteConverger.unsafe_lock_bypass/1 lift the cooldown for every version of that package and of every package the locked release depends on, so that mix deps.update can move off the unsafe release. Retiring a release needs the same package owner permission as publishing one. An attacker who publishes a malicious release can retire the currently locked release, and the next mix deps.update that unlocks the package selects the new release regardless of its age. Hex.Registry.Cooldown.versions/2 checks the bypass by package name alone, so the bypass also covers packages with the same name in other repositories. Cooldown configured through an organization dependency policy is not affected.

This issue affects hex: from 2.5.0 before 2.5.2.
Improper input validation in Microsoft Office SharePoint allows an authorized attacker to disclose information over a network.

Git LFS is a Git extension for versioning large files. From 1.3.0 until 3.8.1, Git LFS does not correctly filter the limited set of options permitted in a repository's .lfsconfig file when option keys contain certain additional components. Crafted keys can mimic options that configure Git LFS to use a custom command to transfer objects, causing Git LFS to execute an attacker-selected command or binary while fetching objects. This issue is fixed in version 3.8.1.

League CommonMark from 1.3.0 before 2.10.2 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows users posting Markdown to bypass the DisallowedRawHtml extension by ending raw HTML with a bare disallowed tag name. Attackers can place a lone <script or <iframe line followed by a block supplying attributes like src or onload, executing stored scripts in viewers' browsers under default GFM settings.

Externally-Generated Error Message Containing Sensitive Information vulnerability in plug_crypto in elixir-plug plug_crypto allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to expose the secret key base through application logs via a wrong-typed argument. Every public function in Plug.Crypto validates argument types in a function-head guard. A failed guard makes the Erlang VM raise FunctionClauseError with the actual argument values in the top stack frame, so the secret key base, a derived key, or the value an API key is compared against lands in that frame. The library's rescue blocks and Plug.Crypto.prune_args_from_stacktrace/1 only reach exceptions raised inside a function body, so they never see a guard failure. Plug.Cowboy and Bandit write the frame to the error log and attach it as crash_reason Logger metadata, which error trackers forward.

Two entry points take request data. Plug.Crypto.verify/4 exposes the secret key base when the token is neither a binary nor nil, which Phoenix.Token.verify/4 reaches because it forwards the token unguarded. Plug.Crypto.secure_compare/2 exposes the other operand when one side is not a binary, as happens when a missing request header yields nil. Reading the leaked value needs separate access to the logs or the error tracker, so the request alone does not disclose the secret to the attacker.

This issue affects plug: from 1.6.3 before 1.7.0; plug_crypto: from 1.0.0 before 2.2.1.

Mattermost versions 11.8.x <= 11.8.0, 11.7.x <= 11.7.3, 11.6.x <= 11.6.5, 11.2.x <= 11.2.4, 10.11.x <= 10.11.20 fail to bound the time and resource consumption of server-side document content extraction which allows an authenticated user with file-upload permission to degrade file uploads for all users on the server via repeatedly uploading small documents that are cheap to upload but expensive to extract, saturating the shared extraction worker pool. Mattermost Advisory ID: MMSA-2026-00694

Mongoose Embedded Web Server / Networking Library before 7.24 contains a WebSocket fragmentation validation vulnerability that allows remote attackers to spoof message metadata by sending a single CONTINUATION frame with FIN=1 as the first data frame instead of a required TEXT/BINARY start frame, violating RFC 6455 sequencing rules. Attackers can craft this malformed frame to make mg_ws_cb() in src/ws.c misinterpret the first byte of payload as saved FIN/opcode flags, causing the application to receive a dispatched MG_EV_WS_MSG event with attacker-controlled flags and data truncated by one byte without closing the connection.

HortusFox (hortusfox-web) through 6.4 contains an unrestricted file upload vulnerability in PlantAttachmentModel that allows authenticated users to store files with client-supplied extensions under public/attachments/. Attackers can upload HTML or SVG files via /plants/attachments/add for stored cross-site scripting, or PHP files where .htaccess is unenforced to execute code.

A security vulnerability has been detected in bleenco abstruse up to 2.1.0. This issue affects the function filepath.Join of the file server/api/worker/download_cache.go of the component Cache Endpoint. Such manipulation of the argument File leads to path traversal. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

FreeRDP 3.10.0 before 3.33.0 contains a heap buffer overflow in the WinPR png_write_data callback that writes past the buffer after a realloc failure. A malicious RDP clipboard peer can supply a large CF_DIB image that triggers out-of-bounds memcpy during PNG conversion, causing a client crash.

PHP uses longjmp() for out-of-memory (OOM) errors to exit the current context and abort handling of the request. Some contexts may not properly account for this scenario and leave request memory in an uninitialized state before performing an allocation. The subsequent request cleanup procedure may read or branch on this memory. Multiple OOM strategies can consistently trigger this condition and lead to remote code execution (RCE).

PHP has various global state that temporarily points into request memory. In some scenarios, global state may not be correctly reset, or may be repopulated after being reset. The global state may then refer to request memory even after it has been freed. Subsequent requests may read or branch on this stale state before it is fully initialized. Multiple strategies can trigger this condition and produce remote code execution (RCE).

Improper Validation of Specified Quantity in Input vulnerability in the Elixir standard library's URI module allows an attacker who supplies a URL to cause a denial of service through CPU exhaustion.

URI.parse/1 converts the port component with String.to_integer/1 in split_authority/1 (lib/elixir/lib/uri.ex) without bounding its length, so a port of up to 1,262,592 decimal digits produces a bignum of that size and a longer one raises SystemLimitError. Rendering the parsed URI back to text (URI.to_string/1, inspect/1, logging, error formatting) converts the bignum with :erlang.integer_to_binary/1, which is quadratic on Erlang/OTP 27, 28 and 29.0: a 400,000-digit port renders in about 2.6 seconds and a 1 MB port in about 18 seconds. Ports above 65535 are also accepted.

This issue affects elixir: from 0.5.0 before 1.18.6, from 1.19.0-rc.0 before 1.19.7, and from 1.20.0-rc.0 before 1.20.5.

A flaw was found in gnome-remote-desktop as shipped in Red Hat Enterprise Linux. In the VNC TLS I/O handlers, retryable GnuTLS results (GNUTLS_E_AGAIN and GNUTLS_E_INTERRUPTED) are handled with an unbounded busy loop instead of yielding to the event loop. A remote attacker who can reach an enabled VNC TLS listener can cause the event-loop thread to spin at high CPU with no forward progress, resulting in denial of service.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in Elementor Elementor Website Builder elementor allows Reflected XSS.This issue affects Elementor Website Builder: from n/a through 4.4.0.
Use of uninitialized memory when processing certain font files in X.Org libXfont before 2.0.10 could be used by authenticated attackers to crash the X server.

NLTK before 3.10.4 contains a path traversal vulnerability in WekaClassifier that allows attackers to bypass nltk.pathsec containment by supplying unvalidated model paths. Attackers controlling the model_filename or model argument can make the weka JVM write files via -d or probe files via -l outside allowed data roots.

In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 2.1 through 2.1.2, a listener configured with `protocol websockets` mishandles empty WebSocket data frames. `net__read_ws()` in `lib/net_ws.c` returns the number of framing bytes consumed (the 4 masking-key bytes) for a data frame with a zero-length payload, without writing any bytes to the caller’s buffer. The MQTT packet reader in `packet__read_single()` (`lib/packet_mosq.c`) trusts that return value as a payload byte count. A remote client can therefore advance the read position over an uninitialised heap allocation, causing the broker to process and forward uninitialised heap memory (information disclosure, including heap and libc pointers), and can underflow the unsigned `to_process` counter so that subsequent attacker-controlled frame data is written past the end of the allocation (heap out-of-bounds write). The out-of-bounds write is reachable from the CONNECT packet before any authentication check, so an unauthenticated client can corrupt the heap and crash the broker even when `allow_anonymous false` is set. Combining the disclosure and the write allows remote code execution as the broker’s user by any client able to establish a session.

Insufficient Session Expiration vulnerability in the Apache Iggy server HTTP transport. A self-issued JSON Web Token (JWT) identified the user only by numeric user ID, and a new user takes the lowest free ID. After an administrator deleted a user, that user's unexpired token, or a token refreshed from it while the ID was free, authenticated as the next account created with that ID and had that account's permissions. Only deployments with HTTP enabled are affected.

This issue affects Apache Iggy: through 0.9.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.10.0, which fixes the issue.

Kan 0.5.5 through 0.7.0 contains an unauthenticated server-side request forgery vulnerability in the /api/download/attatchment route due to an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-32255. When S3_ENDPOINT is unset, attackers can pass arbitrary url query parameters to fetch() to read internal services, localhost ports, and cloud instance metadata.

Improper Session Invalidation after Authentication Credential Change vulnerability in team-alembic ash_authentication allows an attacker holding a victim's session token to stay signed in after the victim resets or changes their password.

With apply_on_password_change? true, AshAuthentication.AddOn.LogOutEverywhere.Transformer adds OnPasswordChange to update actions as a global change guarded by where: changing(hashed_password). That condition is evaluated before the action's before_action hooks run, but AshAuthentication.Strategy.Password.HashPasswordChange sets the new hash in a before_action hook, so for every non-atomic password change the condition is false and the user's stored tokens are not revoked. The generated password reset action and the installer's change_password action are both non-atomic.

This issue affects ash_authentication: from 4.5.0 before 4.15.1 and from 5.0.0-rc.0 before 5.0.0-rc.16.

unarr before 1.2.0 contains a heap-based out-of-bounds read in zip_parse_extra_fields() in zip/parse-zip.c due to an incorrect ZIP64 extra field length check. Attackers can supply a crafted ZIP archive with 0xFFFFFFFF sentinel values and a truncated ZIP64 record to read past the heap buffer and crash the process.

Dell Alienware Command Center (AWCC), versions prior to 6.14.105.0, contain an Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Arbitrary Code Execution and Elevation of Privilege.

Dell Alienware Command Center (AWCC), versions prior to 6.14.105.0, contain an Incorrect Default Permissions vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Arbitrary Code Execution and Elevation of Privilege.

Dell Alienware Command Center (AWCC), versions prior to 6.14.105.0, contain an Improper Authorization in Handler for Custom URL Scheme vulnerability. An unauthenticated attacker with remote access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Command Execution and Launch of Phishing Attacks.

Dell Alienware Command Center (AWCC), versions prior to 6.14.105.0, contain a Least Privilege Violation vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Elevation of Privilege and Denial of Service.

Dell Alienware Command Center (AWCC), versions prior to 6.14.105.0, contain a Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Arbitrary Code Execution.

Dell Alienware Command Center (AWCC), versions prior to 6.14.105.0, contain a Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with local access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Code Execution and Elevation of Privilege.

Multiple products produced by Ruijie Networks Co., Ltd. contain an OS command injection vulnerability that may lead to arbitrary OS commands being executed by an attacker with the administrative privilege.

When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured as a mail proxy, undisclosed traffic can cause a use-after-free in an nginx worker process. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact:
A remote unauthenticated attacker may crash an nginx worker process or corrupt its memory, disrupting service. Remote code execution is a potential impact. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Trigger.dev through 4.8.8 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the supervisor workload server that allows workloads to manipulate runs belonging to other deployments without ownership verification. Attackers with network access and a valid run/snapshot pair can call the attempts/start endpoint to obtain resolved environment variables and run JWTs, or start, complete, and suspend other tenants' runs.

Etherpad is a real-time collaborative editor. From 1.8.14 until 3.3.3, the pre-authentication /static/* plugin asset handler in src/node/utils/Minify.ts performs a backslash-to-forward-slash conversion after src/node/utils/sanitizePathname.ts has completed its POSIX path checks. On POSIX systems the sanitizer correctly treats backslashes as ordinary filename bytes, but the later conversion turns encoded backslash-separated parent-directory segments into traversal components without revalidation or containment. The expressPreSession registration and the always-present ep_etherpad-lite core pseudo-plugin make this path reachable without credentials, allowing a remote attacker to read any file available to the Etherpad process. Disclosed configuration or environment secrets can expose administrator credentials, after which the administrator plugin installer can provide in-process code execution and full server compromise. This issue is fixed in version 3.3.3.

The fix for  CVE-2026-23903 https://shiro.apache.org/security-reports.html#cve_2026_23903  was incomplete for manually-created ShiroFilterFactoryBean, which still matched paths case-sensitively by default.
This issue affects Apache Shiro version 3.0.1, only when ShiroFilterFactoryBean is created manually by the application and static files are served from a case-insensitive filesystem.
Applications that let Shiro Spring (Boot) Starter create the bean are not affected.

Mitigation: Upgrade to version 3.0.2 or later, which fixes the issue.
Alternatively, call setCaseInsensitive(true) on the ShiroFilterFactoryBean.

Vulnerability in the Oracle BI Publisher product of Oracle Analytics (component: Web Server).   The supported version that is affected is 12.2.1.4.0. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows unauthenticated attacker with network access via HTTP to compromise Oracle BI Publisher.  Successful attacks require human interaction from a person other than the attacker and while the vulnerability is in Oracle BI Publisher, attacks may significantly impact additional products (scope change). Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized update, insert or delete access to some of Oracle BI Publisher accessible data as well as  unauthorized read access to a subset of Oracle BI Publisher accessible data. Improper Validation of Specified Quantity in Input vulnerability in the Elixir standard library's JSON module allows an unauthenticated attacker who supplies a JSON document to cause a denial of service through CPU and memory exhaustion.

JSON.decode/1 and JSON.decode!/1 convert each integer literal with erlang:binary_to_integer/1 and do not bound its length. A literal of one million digits decodes successfully but costs 100 to 300 times as much CPU as a string of the same length, so one request body of a few megabytes holds a scheduler for about a second. A literal of more than about 1.29 million digits raises SystemLimitError. Applications generated by phx.new decode request bodies with JSON in Plug.Parsers, before routing and authentication.

This issue affects elixir: from 1.18.0-rc.0 before 1.18.6, from 1.19.0-rc.0 before 1.19.7, and from 1.20.0-rc.0 before 1.20.5.

@fastify/static is the Fastify plugin for serving static files. In versions before 10.1.8, the allowedPath guard receives only the requested pathname, but the underlying send step selects the file to serve afterwards, so a request for a directory resolves to its default index file and an extensionless request resolves through the configured extensions to a matching file. The selected file is streamed without being re-checked against allowedPath, so a guard that denies a specific file is bypassed by requesting its directory or extensionless form. An unauthenticated client can read files inside the static root that the application meant to keep private whenever the denied file is reachable as a directory index or an extension match. The issue is fixed in @fastify/static 10.1.8, and users should upgrade to 10.1.8 or later. As a workaround, also deny the directory and extensionless forms in allowedPath, or disable the index and extensions options.

Session serializer mismatch can lead to remote code execution.

Session upload progress, when enabled, can store attacker-controlled data in a session key using the php_binary or php_serialize session serializer. If the same session is later read with the php serializer, because session.serialize_handler is changed at runtime or differs between applications sharing a session store, bytes inside the key can be passed to the unserializer. A remote attacker able to submit a multipart upload can inject objects, which may lead to code execution when the reading application contains a suitable gadget chain, or to session corruption or denial of service.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

storyblok-backup is an npx CLI tool to create backups of a Storyblok space and restore individual resources. Prior to 0.7.1, the writeJson function used the editable Storyblok component name field as a filename without path containment. A person with component-management access in a Storyblok space could store a component name containing path traversal sequences; when another user later ran a backup for that space, the stored name escaped the configured backup directory and caused a JSON file to be written outside it on the backup host. Depending on the path chosen and the backup process's permissions, this could overwrite existing files at attacker-chosen locations. The vulnerability is specific to components: stories and datasources use numeric identifiers, and asset names are reduced to a final path segment. This issue is fixed in version 0.7.1.

Go-Guerrilla SMTP Daemon is a lightweight SMTP server written in Go. In 1.6.7 and earlier, according to the repository advisory's structured affected range, server.go defines the seven-byte cmdXCLIENT token, but the XCLIENT handler slices input[8:] after matching only that seven-byte verb, so a bare command causes an out-of-bounds panic in handleClient and terminates the daemon because that connection goroutine does not recover the panic. The issue is reachable by an unauthenticated client when the non-default xclient_on setting is enabled; no HELO command is required. The repository fix is present in version 1.6.7-1.
