Apache WSS4J remembers the UsernameToken Nonce, the Timestamp and signature of a signed message, and the ID of a SAML 2.0 "OneTimeUse" assertion, so that a captured message cannot be accepted twice. It checked whether a value had already been seen, validated the message, and only then remembered the value, as two separate steps. If several copies of the same message were processed at the same time, they could all pass the check before any of them was remembered, and all be accepted. An attacker who obtained a valid message before the recipient first processed it could send several copies at once, so that the same authenticated request was executed more than once. Where a UsernameToken is not bound to the message by a signature, the copies could carry different message bodies. The attacker needs to obtain the message while it is still in transit; a message captured after it has been accepted cannot be replayed. Affects deployments with a replay cache configured, as Apache CXF has by default. The value is now checked and remembered in a single atomic step. Custom ReplayCache implementations should override the new ReplayCache.addIfAbsent method with an operation that is atomic in their underlying store. Users are recommended to upgrade to versions 4.0.3 or 3.0.7 or 2.4.5, which fix this issue.
Dell PowerStore SDNAS contains a path traversal vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated attacker to read, modify, or delete arbitrary files on the NAS node.
Dell PowerStore SDNAS contains a buffer overflow vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to cause a denial of service or potential code execution on the NAS node.

Electrum before 4.8.3 fails to verify signatures of wallet-owned inputs in unconfirmed mempool transactions, allowing malicious servers to replace a just-broadcast transaction with a conflicting one. Attackers can swallow the user's transaction and display an invalid zero-fee copy paying an attacker address, tricking users into RBF fee-bumping and signing it.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in phoenixframework phoenix_html allows an attacker who controls attribute names to inject attributes and script into rendered HTML via Phoenix.HTML.attributes_escape/1.

attributes_escape/1 in lib/phoenix_html.ex escapes attribute values but not attribute names. key_escape/1 passes a binary key through html_escape, which neutralizes quotes and angle brackets but not whitespace, so a key such as x onmouseover ends the attribute and starts a new one. An atom key is only dasherized, so any character passes, including quotes and >. Nested data, aria and phx keys take the same paths. An application is affected when it builds attribute keys from untrusted input and renders them through HEEx <tag {@attrs}>, content_tag/3, or a direct call. Before 3.0.0 the same code lived in Phoenix.HTML.Tag.

This issue affects phoenix_html: from 1.0.0 before 3.3.5 and from 4.0.0 before 4.4.0.

The InfoScan Electron desktop client improperly handles TLS certificate errors by accepting certificates without validating their trustworthiness. The client also configures Electron with nodeIntegration enabled, contextIsolation disabled, and webSecurity disabled. These settings weaken the client’s security boundaries. An attacker who is able to intercept or manipulate network communications may be able to present an untrusted certificate without the application rejecting the connection.

In Progress® Telerik® Document Processing Libraries prior to version 2026.3.1027, improper verification of cryptographic signatures and improper certificate validation in RadPdfProcessing digital signature validation allow an unauthenticated attacker to cause signature validation to report forged content as unmodified and its signing certificate as valid via a crafted signed PDF document.

The My Calendar – Accessible Event Manager plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'event_title' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.8.13 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires the plugin's documented permission grant to be applied, which allows Subscriber-level users to add and publish events; once granted, a self-submitted event title containing an entity-encoded payload is auto-published and fires in any visitor's browser upon clicking the event on the public calendar.

Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File vulnerability in the Apache Iggy server. If Apache Iggy 0.9.0 started without IGGY_ROOT_USERNAME and IGGY_ROOT_PASSWORD, it generated a root password and wrote it to the server log file, which is enabled by default. The system snapshot command (GetSnapshot on the binary transports and POST /snapshot on HTTP) let a user with only the read_servers permission download the server log files. That user could read the generated root password and log in as root.

This issue affects Apache Iggy: 0.9.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.10.0, which fixes the issue. Version 0.10.0 never generates a root password, and the snapshot requires the manage_servers permission. If a 0.9.0 server generated its root password, change that password.

The Video & Photo Gallery for Ultimate Member plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Deletion in versions up to, and including, 1.1.4 This is due to the um_gallery_add_videos() AJAX handler persisting user-supplied videos[] values into the file_name column after only esc_url() — which preserves path-traversal sequences — and the companion um_gallery_delete_photo() helper passing that stored value to unlink() through get_user_image_path() with no canonicalization or allowed-directory check. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to delete arbitrary files on the server, which can be leveraged to achieve remote code execution when the right file (such as wp-config.

When using the listen directive with the ssl parameter in the http block with TLSv1.3 enabled, an attacker can use a specially crafted TLS connection to cause an infinite loop in the NGINX worker process while reading the HTTP request body. As a result, the worker process stops accepting new connections and processing existing connections. Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Impact: This vulnerability allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) of NGINX. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Authorization bypass through a user-controlled key in the PuppetDB facts terminus used by Puppet Server allows a client holding any valid agent certificate to overwrite the facts, including trusted facts, that PuppetDB stores for a different node. In Puppet Enterprise deployments where task permissions are scoped to node groups defined by facts or trusted facts, this can allow a user to run tasks on nodes outside their permitted scope.

The My Calendar – Accessible Event Manager plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'mc_template (template body); event_title (payload storage)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.8.13 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires the site to have granted mc_add_events to Subscriber-level users (a configurable plugin permission), and relies on a privileged user — such as an Administrator — following the event preview link surfaced on the My Calendar Events management screen.

CakePHP 4.5.12, 4.6.5, 5.1.8 through 5.1.10, 5.2.14 through 5.2.15, 5.3.7, and 5.4.0 through 5.4.3 contain an email header injection vulnerability because SmtpTransport and MailTransport strip only CRLF pairs from header values, an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-77634. Attackers controlling custom headers set via Message::setHeaders() or Message::addHeaders() can insert a bare CR or LF to inject headers like Bcc, redirecting or altering outgoing mail.

Incorrect default permissions in the ASUS DisplayWidget Center allow a local, low-privileged user to achieve arbitrary code execution in the security context of another user via a crafted executable placed in that user-writable directory, which the application launches when the other user runs it and uses a particular feature.Refer to the '
Security Update for ASUS Display Widget Center ' section on the ASUS Security Advisory for more information.

A flaw was found in GIMP. The PSD plug-in’s image resource header loader uses an incorrect destination size when copying a converted resource name into a fixed stack buffer. Opening a crafted PSD file can cause a stack-based buffer overflow, leading to a crash and potentially arbitrary code execution.

The NextGEN Gallery plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting in versions up to, and including, 4.5.5 via the 'ajax_pagination_referrer' request parameter used on the /ngg_tag/<tag>/ taxonomy page. This is due to the plugin reading the pagination base URL from $_REQUEST, preserving the attacker-supplied host on the tag route (where ngg_wprouting_add_post_permalink is forced to false so the plugin does not re-base the links to the site's own permalink), and caching the fully rendered page in a transient keyed only on the request URI (not the request body) for 1800 seconds via NGG_RENDERING_CACHE / PHOTOCRATI_CACHE. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to poison the cached /ngg_tag/<tag>/ page so that its pagination links point to an attacker-controlled host; the plugin's own ajax_pagination.

The publicly distributed InfoScan Electron installer contains configuration files identifying hostnames associated with customer installations and internal development, testing, and database infrastructure. An individual who obtains and inspects the installer can extract these hostnames without authenticating to the affected systems.

InfoScan uses hard-coded cryptographic keys and initialization-vector values in its database-encryption implementation. The application uses these values to encrypt the MongoDB password before storing it in the Windows registry. Because the cryptographic material is embedded in the distributed application, an individual with access to the encrypted registry value and the application code may be able to recover the database password.

InfoScan does not enforce authentication on an endpoint used to retrieve sales-automation templates. A local attacker can submit an HTTP request to the affected endpoint without a valid session and retrieve the returned template data.

InfoScan contains an unauthenticated information disclosure vulnerability in its mobile-enumeration and version-reporting endpoints. A remote attacker can send HTTP requests without authentication to retrieve system configuration information, including usernames and display names, multifactor authentication configuration status, session settings, application version information, server details, hardware module firmware versions, and the BACnet/IP port used by the installation.

Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling vulnerability in Plug.Parsers.MULTIPART in elixir-plug plug allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to exhaust memory via a multipart request body built from parts without headers, or from header lines without a name and a value. The parser charges the :length limit only with the name and value bytes of each part header and the bytes of each part body. The part delimiter, the header separator, and the line endings cost nothing.

In lib/plug/parsers/multipart.ex, Plug.Parsers.MULTIPART.parse_multipart_headers/5 keeps an entry for every part without a content-disposition header, together with its header list, until the whole body is read. A request made of such parts does not reach the limit at any size, and the parser process holds a multiple of the request size in memory until parsing completes. Any endpoint that uses Plug.Parsers with the :multipart parser is reachable.

This issue affects plug: from 1.13.0 before 1.20.4.

Incorrect Authorization vulnerability in the devices page bulk move in nerves-hub nerves_hub_web allows an authenticated user with the manage role in one organization and only the view role in another to move devices into the second organization's product via the "Move device(s) to product" action. The target-product event in NervesHubWeb.Live.Devices.Index looks the product up with NervesHub.Products.get_by_id/2, which checks that the user is a member of the product's organization at any role, and move-devices-product then changes each selected device's organization and product. The device API's move requires manage in the target organization, and an earlier fix added the check on the organization the devices leave but not on the one they enter.

A moved device keeps its key and certificate, joins the target organization's matching deployment groups, and is sent their firmware with a download URL, which the view role cannot otherwise obtain. The user cannot change or control devices that already belong to the other organization.

This issue affects nerves_hub: from 1.0.0 before 2.5.3.

InfoScan fails to properly handle certain malformed or incomplete requests to its login and password-reset endpoints. These requests can trigger unhandled server exceptions that return detailed Node.js stack traces to the requester. The responses disclose internal filesystem paths, application directory names, source file locations, and line numbers.

The built-in regular expression name finder for latitude and longitude coordinates uses a pattern that is vulnerable to excessive backtracking. An attacker who can supply text that an application analyzes with this name finder can cause high CPU consumption, leading to denial of service. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.5.13 or 3.0.0, which fix the issue.

The Toocheke Companion plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'meta[<meta_id>][value]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.39 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with author-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is possible because omitting the comic_blog_post_editor field from the POST request bypasses the plugin's sanitization callback entirely, causing WordPress core to store the raw payload byte-for-byte via update_post_meta().

The Charitable – Donation & Fundraising Platform (Donation Forms, Recurring Donations & Fundraising Campaigns) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'stripe_payment_method' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.8.15.1 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The nonce required to reach the nopriv AJAX endpoint is publicly obtainable from any rendered campaign donation form, making exploitation trivially accessible to unauthenticated visitors on sites with Stripe configured as a payment gateway.

In Eclipse Ditto versions 1.1.0 to 3.9.8, when pre-authentication is enabled, the gateway service accepts the pre-authenticated subject not only from the `x-ditto-pre-authenticated` HTTP header set by a trusted reverse proxy, but also from an undocumented `x-ditto-pre-authenticated` URL query parameter that a client can set. A reverse proxy that only overwrites the header therefore does not stop clients from supplying their own subject. With the default configuration of the Ditto Helm chart (`global.jwtOnly: false`, which implicitly enables pre-authentication), the bundled nginx skips HTTP Basic authentication for any request with an `Authorization: Bearer` header and forwards it without the pre-authentication header. An unauthenticated remote attacker can send an invalid Bearer token together with the query parameter to authenticate as any chosen policy subject. Pre-authentication succeeds before the JWT is validated, so the attacker can read and modify Things and Policies with that subject's permissions. As a mitigation, disable pre-authentication in the gateway (`ENABLE_PRE_AUTHENTICATION=false`) or, when using the Helm chart, configure `global.jwtOnly: true`.
Verifying a maliciously crafted CMS or PKCS#7 SignedData message with CRL checking enabled may consume excessive CPU time, growing with the square of the message size.

The My Calendar – Accessible Event Manager plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'event_post (post ID) + event_title (XSS payload) + content (shortcode)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.8.13 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This requires an administrator to have granted the mc_add_events capability to Subscriber-level or other lower-privileged roles, which is the plugin's documented workflow for allowing front-end event submissions.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in WP Chill Gallery PhotoBlocks photoblocks-grid-gallery allows Stored XSS.This issue affects Gallery PhotoBlocks: from n/a through 1.3.8.

Use of cache containing sensitive information vulnerability in Apache Tomcat's ExpiresFilter caused by the filter removing cache-control header fields set by the authentication layer.



This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.27, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.61, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.123.



The following versions were EOL at the time the CVE was created but are known to be affected: from 8.5.0 through 8.5.100, from 7.0.1 through 7.0.109. Older unsupported versions may also be affected.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.29, 10.1.62 or 9.0.124, which fix the issue.
Note: Tomcat 11.0.28 was not released

The CWILL (Formerly ParcelPanel) – Shipment Tracking, Tracking & Order Tracking for WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'data[].courier_code, data[].tracking_number (plus pp_sign for the auth bypass)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.6.2 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The authentication bypass is reachable only when the parcelpanel_api_key WordPress option is non-empty, which occurs automatically once an admin has opened or connected the ParcelPanel admin page; at that point any unauthenticated attacker can bypass the sole access gate by supplying a JSON boolean true as pp_sign, which PHP's loose == operator coerces to true when compared against the non-empty md5 hex string.

Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification) vulnerability in elixir-grpc grpc_core and grpc allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust server memory via a compressed Erlang external term in a gRPC message body.

GRPC.Codec.Erlpack.decode/2 (grpc_core/lib/grpc/codec/erlpack.ex, and lib/grpc/codec/erlpack.ex before the package split) passes the message body to :erlang.binary_to_term/2. That function inflates a compressed term in full before it returns. The codec sets no limit on the decoded size, and its type checks run only on the decoded term. The server's max_body_size limit counts the compressed bytes of the request. A request with Content-Type: application/grpc+erlpack can therefore make the server allocate a term much larger than the request body.

This issue affects grpc: from 0.4.0 before 1.0.0; grpc_core: from 1.0.0 before 1.1.0.

Description:
This issue affects NGINX Plus and NGINX Open Source configurations that use HTTP/3. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can cause a use-after-free condition in the NGINX worker process, leading to a restart. Exploitation also depends on conditions beyond the attacker’s control. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact:
This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system or to possibly trigger a code execution. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

FreeRDP before 3.32.2 has a heap out-of-bounds write in the RDPGFX client because the delete_surface callback truncates surface hash keys to 16 bits, leaving the surface table inconsistent so HashTable_GetKeys writes past its allocated key array. A malicious or man-in-the-middle RDP server can exploit this by creating surfaceId 0xFFFF, closing the RDPGFX channel, sending repeated DELETESURFACE PDUs, and then sending ENDFRAME or RESETGRAPHICS.

Budibase is an open-source low-code platform. Prior to 3.50.0, the public POST /api/global/users/init endpoint on a self-hosted single-tenant deployment accepts an attacker-controlled tenantId and evaluates checkAnyUserExists() in the selected tenant database instead of the legitimate default tenant. An unauthenticated attacker can select an unused tenant namespace to bypass the one-time initialization guard, causing packages/worker/src/api/controllers/global/users.ts to create a tenant-specific CouchDB database and a global-administrator document without a session or CSRF token. Repeating this operation with unique tenant identifiers can exhaust datastore resources and leave latent privileged records. The created administrator cannot log into the default tenant while multi-tenancy remains disabled, which limits the immediate impact to persistent writes, denial of service, and records that may become usable during later multi-tenant operation or migration. This issue is fixed in versions 3.50.0 and 4.0.0.

Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection') vulnerability in PublishPress PublishPress Authors publishpress-authors allows Blind SQL Injection.This issue affects PublishPress Authors: from n/a through 4.18.0.

This issue affects NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source configurations that use HTTP/2. When NGINX processes undisclosed traffic, the flow control window can exceed the allowed threshold, potentially resulting in a heap buffer overflow typically followed by an NGINX worker segmentation fault. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact: An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to crash the NGINX worker process, corrupt its memory, or potentially execute code remotely. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

The web installer of JTL-Shop executes its
state-changing installation tasks without checking whether the shop is already
installed, and was not removed or locked after the installation. An unauthenticated
remote attacker who can reach the installer directory can supply their own
database credentials, create administrator and synchronisation accounts and
overwrite the shop configuration. This can lead to a full takeover of
the shop, including code execution on the server.

HomeBox is a home inventory and organization system. Prior to 0.27.0, the unauthenticated GET /swagger/doc.json endpoint copies the client-supplied X-Forwarded-Host header into the OpenAPI host field without requiring a trusted proxy or validating the value. An attacker can therefore make the served OpenAPI document direct Swagger UI Try it out requests to an attacker-controlled host. When a shared cache or CDN stores and serves that poisoned document to an authenticated user, Swagger UI sends the user's API requests and bearer token to the attacker, enabling disclosure and modification of the user's HomeBox data. Without a shared cache, the attacker can affect only the attacker's own response. This issue is fixed in version 0.27.0.

HomeBox is a home inventory and organization system. Prior to 0.27.0, a HomeBox password change revokes the user's other session tokens but does not revoke the user's API keys, and API keys have no default API-key expiration. An attacker who has obtained an API key can therefore retain full API-level access after the account owner changes the password and can keep that access indefinitely unless the owner discovers and manually deletes the key by ID. Because the password change terminates other sessions, the surviving API credential can evade the owner's expected containment and detection. This issue is fixed in version 0.27.0.

Hickory DNS hickory-recursor 0.25.0-alpha.3 through 0.25.2 and hickory-resolver 0.26.0-alpha.1 before 0.26.2 contains a query amplification vulnerability in its recursive resolver, which mishandles cyclic sibling name server referrals that lack glue records. Attackers controlling two zones whose name servers reference each other without glue records can make the recursor loop, sending many upstream queries, amplified further by zero-TTL NS records.

When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured to use HTTP/2 for client connections and proxy client requests to a backend, a specially crafted request can result in use-after-free in the worker process, if this process is running low on worker_connections. Additionally, attackers can execute code on systems with Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) disabled or when the attacker can bypass ASLR.




Impact:



This vulnerability may allow remote attackers to cause a denial-of-service (DoS) on the NGINX system or may allow a code execution. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

This issue occurs when NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured as a proxy, the proxied server name includes variables, and a Server Side Includes (SSI) or mirror directive sends a subrequest to a location that resolves the same server name. Under these conditions, a specially crafted HTTP request may cause a use-after-free condition in a worker process. An attacker may also be able to execute code if Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR) is disabled or the attacker can bypass ASLR.

Impact: 
An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to crash the NGINX worker process, corrupt its memory, or perform remote code execution (RCE)



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

Description
When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured with the ngx_stream_ssl_preread_module module, a specially crafted ClientHello message from an unauthenticated attacker causes forged values of the ngx_stream_ssl_preread_module variables, affecting virtual server selection. In addition, it may also cause a disagreement with a proxied server terminating the SSL/TLS connection without Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.3 support.

Impact
This vulnerability may allow an attacker to forge values of the ngx_stream_ssl_preread_module variables and bypass the NGINX systems stream routing segmentation. As a result, the attacker may be able to route the connection to a privileged or internal backend that should be unreachable and gain access to sensitive information. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.






Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

A use-after-free in Node.js HTTP/2 stream teardown can leak response memory, including the contents of other connections' response buffers, to a peer. When a stream is torn down while a write is still backpressured, for example by a peer `RST_STREAM` or by the server's own per-stream timeout destroying the stream, the stream's response buffer is freed but a reference to it is still used, so freed or unrelated heap memory is written to the socket instead of the intended response. On Node.js 26.x and 24.x the teardown can be driven purely by a remote peer once the window-size change from 26.9.0 and 24.22.0 is present, and on all supported lines the same defect is reachable through an application-initiated teardown such as a per-stream idle timeout. This vulnerability affects Node.js 26.x, 24.x, and 22.x.

SDDC Manager contains an SQL-injection vulnerability due to improper sanitization of user-supplied input.
Affected versions: 9.1.x.x (fixed in 9.1.1.0200); 9.0.x.x (fixed in 9.0.2.0100); 5.x (fixed in 5.2.5).

SDDC Manager contains an authenticated command-injection vulnerability due to improper sanitization of user-supplied input.
Affected versions: 9.1.x.x (fixed in 9.1.1.0200); 9.0.x.x (fixed in 9.0.2.0100); 5.x (fixed in 5.2.5).

SDDC Manager contains a local privilege-escalation vulnerability.
Affected versions: 9.1.x.x (fixed in 9.1.1.0200); 9.0.x.x (fixed in 9.0.2.0100); 5.x (fixed in 5.2.5).

VMware Tools for Windows contains a SAML token signature bypass vulnerability.
Affected versions: 13.x.x.x (fixed in 13.1.5.0); 12.3.x (fixed in 12.5.5).

The Slimbox Plugin plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'el.title (HTML-decoded title attribute of a stored <a rel^=lightbox> element)' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires a companion plugin such as bbPress that permits low-privileged users to store anchor elements with arbitrary title and rel attributes, as WordPress core comment handling does not preserve rel on anchor tags by default.

The Pie Register – User Registration, Profiles & Content Restriction plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 3.8.4.17 This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to overwrite the role of the site's primary administrator account (user ID 1) with the registration form's configured role, demoting the administrator to a lower-privileged role and locking them out of wp-admin. This vulnerability is exploitable only on PHP 8+, where casting a WP_Error object to int yields 1, causing the role modification to target user ID 1.

A vulnerability has been found in FlowCI flow-core-x up to 1.23.49. The affected element is the function ConditionManagerImpl.run of the file core/src/main/java/com/flowci/core/common/manager/ConditionManagerImpl.java of the component Groovy Script Evaluation. The manipulation of the argument condition leads to code injection. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A vulnerability was found in FlowCI flow-core-x up to 1.23.49. The impacted element is the function FileHelper.unzip of the file common/src/main/java/com/flowci/common/helper/FileHelper.java. The manipulation results in path traversal. The attack may be performed from remote. A high complexity level is associated with this attack. The exploitability is regarded as difficult. The exploit has been made public and could be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A vulnerability was determined in FlowCI flow-core-x up to 1.23.49. This affects the function exist/save/read/remove of the file store/src/main/java/com/flowci/store/LocalFileManager.java of the component LocalFileManager. This manipulation of the argument fileName causes path traversal. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. A high degree of complexity is needed for the attack. The exploitability is reported as difficult. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

phpMyFAQ 4.1.9 before 4.1.11 and 4.2.0 pre-releases before 4.2.0-beta.3 contain an account enumeration vulnerability in the unauthenticated POST /api/webauthn/prepare-login endpoint, which returns stable stored credential IDs for passkey-registered accounts but an md5(time())-derived fallback ID otherwise. Unauthenticated attackers can compare allowCredentials IDs from requests sent more than one second apart, without rate limiting, to identify existing passkey-registered accounts and their credential IDs.

Authorization omission in the 'admusers' operation of the POST request to '/xmanagercore/api/services/' in XOneManager 3.8.3.0. The API fails to verify the required role for querying the directory. An authenticated member of the project can obtain the list of platform accounts—including administrative accounts—along with details such as email addresses, roles, and associated companies.

The checkout of JTL-Shop stores the delivery address
ID submitted by the customer in the session and adopts it into the order
without verifying that the address belongs to the ordering customer. A remote
attacker with access to the checkout, including a guest, can thereby attach
the delivery address of another customer to their own order. Name and
address of the other customer, and depending on the shop configuration
further contact data, then appear in the order confirmation and customer
account. As the IDs are sequential, addresses can be enumerated. Goods may
also be shipped to the wrong address.

The Optimole – Optimize Images | Convert WebP & AVIF | CDN & Lazy Load | Image Optimization plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 4.2.19 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Exploitation requires the AMP plugin to be active in Transitional or Standard template mode, and comments must be open on the target post, which is the WordPress default.

When NGINX Plus or NGINX Open Source is configured to use the try_files and alias directives with a map variable, certain combinations of regular expression captures in map and try_files can cause a segmentation fault in an NGINX worker process.

Impact:
An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to cause an NGINX worker process to terminate unexpectedly. There is no control plane exposure; this is a data plane issue only.



Note: Software versions which have reached End of Technical Support (EoTS) are not evaluated.

ServiceNow has addressed a code injection security issue that was identified in the ServiceNow AI Platform. This issue could enable an authenticated user with template editing privileges to execute code in the context of another user's session. 


ServiceNow deployed an update to hosted instances, and provided the update to our partners and self-hosted customers. We are not currently aware of malicious exploitation against ServiceNow instances. We recommend customers promptly apply appropriate updates or upgrade to a patched release if they have not already done so.

Ettercap before 0.8.5.1 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in func_pcre() in src/ec_filter.c that reads the PCRE2 ovector after freeing match data. Network-adjacent attackers can send packets matching a loaded pcre_regex() substitution filter to corrupt memory and potentially execute code as root.

Ettercap before 0.8.5.1 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in gg_get_version() in src/dissectors/ec_gg.c that writes up to 44 bytes into a 30-byte allocation. Remote attackers can send Gadu-Gadu traffic on TCP port 8074 with a crafted version field through a monitored network to corrupt heap memory in the Ettercap process, which normally runs as root.

Ettercap before 0.8.5.1 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in sslw_get_clienthello_sni() in src/ec_sslwrap.c that trusts the unchecked 16-bit SNI length field. Network-adjacent attackers can send crafted TLS ClientHello messages during SSL interception to leak up to 64 KB of heap memory upstream or crash Ettercap.

Ettercap before 0.8.5.1 contains an out-of-bounds read and size_t underflow vulnerability in sslw_remove_sts() in src/ec_sslwrap.c, caused by a stale length and an unchecked memmem() result when stripping Strict-Transport-Security headers. A malicious HTTPS server whose response passes through Ettercap's SSL interception can trigger out-of-bounds reads and memory corruption in the Ettercap process, which normally runs as root.

Ettercap before 0.8.5.1 contains an integer underflow in ccmp_decrypt() in src/ec_encryption_ccmp.c that subtracts the 8-byte CCMP trailer without checking minimum length. Attackers on a network whose WPA key is loaded can send a short crafted CCMP frame to overflow a stack buffer in the Ettercap process, which normally runs as root.

Ettercap before 0.8.5.1 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in Parse_NTLM_Auth() in src/dissectors/ec_http.c due to unvalidated NTLM message offsets. Attackers can send a crafted HTTP Authorization header observed by Ettercap to read beyond the buffer, disclosing memory or crashing the process.

Ettercap before 0.8.5.1 contains a stack buffer underwrite vulnerability in the telnet dissector in src/dissectors/ec_telnet.c that decrements the output pointer on backspace without a lower bound check. Attackers can send a telnet stream with more backspaces than preceding characters to write below the stack buffer, corrupting the stack of the Ettercap process that normally runs as root.

A flaw was found in GStreamer's MXF demuxer. When an application processes a crafted MXF file, an off-by-one bounds check can allow a one-byte write past the logical end of a temporal offset array. This may corrupt memory and cause the application to crash. The extent of the impact has not been demonstrated by a runtime test.

A broken access control vulnerability in WatchGuard Dimension's Device Summary feature allows an authenticated, low-privileged user to retrieve a device's detailed summary data by bypassing restrictions that would otherwise hide this information.

In Autonomy Logic OpenPLC Runtime versions 4.2.4 and prior, a race condition allows multiple concurrent requests to pass the existence check before any user is committed, resulting in several unauthenticated admin accounts being created.

n8n before 1.123.89, 2.0.0 before 2.45.5, 2.46.0 before 2.46.1, and 3.0.0 before 3.0.1 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the Chat Trigger that allows unauthenticated attackers to skip n8n User Auth through the setup GET webhook route in embedded chat mode. Attackers can send unauthenticated GET requests to the chat webhook URL to read named session conversation history or trigger workflows with attacker-supplied input.

n8n before 1.123.89, 2.0.0 before 2.45.5, 2.46.0 before 2.46.1, and 3.0.0 before 3.0.1 contains an insufficient isolation vulnerability in workflow expression evaluation that allows authenticated users to escape the sandbox. Attackers with permission to create or modify workflows can craft expressions referencing unexpected JavaScript properties to execute arbitrary code on the n8n host.

OpenEMR before 8.5.0 contains a SQL injection vulnerability that allows any authenticated core user to inject SQL by supplying crafted patient_data field names to the CCR revandapprove controller. Attackers can embed scalar subqueries in the UPDATE patient_data SET clause to read staff password hashes and portal reset values, alter arbitrary patient demographics, and take over patient-portal accounts.

WWBN AVideo 6.5 before 29.8.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to log in as any user via Hybridauth social login display names. Attackers can set their X, Facebook, Yahoo or LinkedIn display name to a victim's username and withhold email, causing login.json.php or oauth2.php to log them in as that account, including administrators, without a password.
In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 2.1.0 to 2.1.2, the mosquitto_ctrl utility would crash if attempting to interact with a hostile broker and the broker sent a non-string "error" value.

In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 2.0.0 to 2.0.22 and 2.1.0 to 2.1.2, the return value of password hash functions for sha512-pbkdf2 and legacy sha512 were not checked. Starting with OpenSSL 4.0, sha512-pbkdf2 hashing will fail when using the FIPS provider for passwords shorter than 8 characters. This has the effect that newly created passwords would match against any other password with fewer than 8 characters.

Partially overwritten session files can lead to remote code execution.

The files session save handler, which is the default, writes updated session data into the existing session file without first clearing it. If a write is interrupted, the file can contain the beginning of the new session followed by the end of the old one, and bytes of an ordinary string can later be unserialized as objects. An attacker who can influence the session data, for example through session upload progress, and interrupt a write at a suitable point may inject objects, which can lead to code execution when the application contains a suitable gadget chain. Session data can also be corrupted.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

The Xagio SEO & AEO – AI SEO for Google Rankings & AI Visibility plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'title' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 7.1.0.51 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The wp_kses_post filter applied at save time does not strip angle-bracket-free double-quote breakout payloads in shortcode attribute values, leaving injected event handlers intact in stored post content.

The Mega Forms – Drag & Drop Form Builder with Multi-Step & Conditional Logic plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to arbitrary file deletion due to insufficient file path validation in the delete_entry function in all versions up to, and including, 1.7.9 This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the server, which can easily lead to remote code execution when the right file is deleted (such as wp-config.php). The attacker-supplied path is stored via the unauthenticated form submission endpoint, but the actual file deletion only occurs when an administrator subsequently deletes the stored entry — a routine housekeeping action that serves as the detonation trigger. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.

Dagu 1.23.0 before 2.0.0 defaults auth.mode to none, allowing unauthenticated attackers to execute OS commands through the /api/v2/dag-runs endpoint. Attackers can send a POST request with an inline spec defining steps containing arbitrary shell commands to achieve remote code execution. Exploitation evidence was first observed by the Shadowserver Foundation on 2026-03-11.

A flaw has been found in H3C ICG2000 Unified Communication Gateway 2023. This issue affects some unknown processing of the file /wnm/check.j of the component Web Management Module. Executing a manipulation can lead to missing authentication. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit has been published and may be used. Upgrading to version R9141PXX is capable of addressing this issue. It is recommended to upgrade the affected component. The vendor confirms: "We have confirmed this issue is a known issue and has been fixed in R9141PXX versions."

In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 1.6 to 2.0.22 and 2.1.0 to 2.1.2, an MQTT v5.0 client connecting with a will-delay-interval that subsequently disconnects with a shorter interval causes all delayed wills to be suppressed.

The glob functions in the GNU C Library versions 2.44 and earlier may free the same heap block twice when a memory allocation fails while glob prepends the directory name to the names it matched.  The names already rewritten are freed, but their pointers stay in the result vector, and the error path frees them again with globfree.

The allocation must fail after at least one name has been rewritten, so the issue can only be reached when the process is already close to its memory limit, for example under an address space limit (RLIMIT_AS) or on a 32-bit system.  The attacker needs control to make the result large enough to make the program or service run out of memory, either by controlling the glob pattern and having knowledge of the filesystem layout or through other means.  This issue affects all architectures and ABIs supported by the GNU C Library.

A maliciously crafted SBSAR file, when imported or loaded through the Substance in 3ds Max plugin in Autodesk 3ds Max, can trigger an Out-of-Bounds Write vulnerability. A malicious actor may leverage this vulnerability to cause an application crash, data corruption, or potentially execute arbitrary code in the context of the current process.

Poste.io is vulnerable to remote code execution in DMARC report processing. Email sent to dmarc-reports@<domain> is saved without sender verification. Script that runs as root unpacks the attachments using unsafe shell commands, allowing command injection through crafted attachments (e.g. file names or archive contents). A remote unauthenticated attacker who can send an email to the server's port 25 can execute arbitrary commands as root within the Poste.io container.


This issue was fixed in version 2.5.22.

@fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server. In versions before 11.6.10, it rejects destinations containing parent-directory path segments by an exact string match, so a segment that carries a semicolon path parameter, such as a dot-dot segment followed by a semicolon and an optional parameter, is not equal to the plain dot-dot form and passes the check, and the WHATWG URL parser keeps it as an ordinary segment so the rewrite-prefix containment check also passes. Servlet containers such as Apache Tomcat and Jetty strip semicolon path parameters from each segment before resolving dot-segments, so a request routed through the configured prefix is rewritten and reaches the upstream where it resolves above the intended subtree, escaping the path the proxy is meant to expose and, on some containers, crossing application contexts. Both the HTTP and WebSocket proxy paths are affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.10, and users should upgrade to 11.6.10 or later.

@fastify/reply-from is a Fastify plugin that forwards requests to an upstream HTTP server. In versions before 12.8.4, its buildURL function rejects parent-directory path segments by an exact string match, so a segment that carries a semicolon path parameter, such as a dot-dot segment followed by a semicolon and an optional parameter, is not equal to the plain dot-dot form and passes the traversal check, and the WHATWG URL parser keeps it as an ordinary segment so the base-prefix containment check also passes. Backends that strip semicolon path parameters before resolving dot-segments, such as Apache Tomcat, Jetty, WildFly, and Spring Boot, turn the segment back into a parent-directory reference and resolve it, so an unauthenticated client can escape the intended upstream prefix and reach internal paths such as admin or internal API endpoints, including with state-changing methods. Deployments that proxy to Node.js, nginx, or Express upstreams are not affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/reply-from 12.8.4, and users should upgrade to 12.8.4 or later.

A flaw was found in the quarkus-rest-jsonb component of Quarkus. An unauthenticated remote attacker can cause a Denial of Service (DoS) by sending HTTP requests containing deeply nested JSON payloads to vulnerable endpoints. The application fails during JSON parsing and records an excessively large error trace for each small request. This disproportionate log amplification can exhaust system disk space or overwhelm log processing pipelines, degrading service availability.

The Events Made Easy plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'event[event_notes]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.3.8 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is only exploitable when the plugin's 'Allow guest submit?' Frontend Submit option is enabled, though the required nonce is freely obtainable by any anonymous visitor as it is printed on every frontend page.

The Nelio Content – Editorial Calendar & Social Media Auto-Posting plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'values' parameter in versions up to, and including, 5.0.1. This is due to the /nelio-content/v1/post/(?P<id>[\d]+)/items REST route registering the 'values' argument with no sanitize_callback, storing values['efiUrl'] raw to the _nelioefi_url post-meta via update_post_meta(), and then interpolating that stored value into a style attribute via generate_style_tag() with no esc_attr/esc_url before splicing it into the img tag emitted by the_post_thumbnail(). This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page.

The Nelio Content – Editorial Calendar & Social Media Auto-Posting plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to authorization bypass in all versions up to, and including, 5.0.1. This is due to the plugin not properly verifying that a user is authorized to perform an action. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to view the titles, publication dates, author display names, and author email addresses (including those of administrators) of private, draft, and pending posts they cannot access, and to write arbitrary _nc_url metadata onto posts they cannot edit.

Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized access to critical data or complete access to all Oracle VM VirtualBox accessible data. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 7.4 (Confidentiality impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:A/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N).

Denial of service through folded HTTP response headers.

The HTTP stream wrapper joins each continuation line of a folded response header to the accumulated value by allocating a new string and copying the whole value, so a response with many short continuation lines takes disproportionate CPU time to parse. An attacker who controls an HTTP or HTTPS response fetched through file_get_contents(), fopen() or other stream functions, by making the application request a chosen URL or by influencing a server it already contacts, can keep PHP workers busy. Repeated or concurrent requests can cause a denial of service.

This issue affects PHP versions from 8.1.32 through 8.1.34, from 8.2.28 before 8.2.36, from 8.3.18 before 8.3.37, from 8.4.5 before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

Mixed-case HTTPS and FTPS URLs can expose data in plaintext.

The HTTP and FTP stream wrappers recognise URL schemes case-insensitively, but enable TLS only when the scheme contains a lowercase "s" at a fixed position. A URL such as HTTPS:// or FTPS:// passed to file_get_contents(), fopen() or other stream functions, or received as an HTTP redirect target, is therefore handled over unencrypted HTTP or FTP. An attacker able to observe the network traffic can read data the application expected TLS to protect, including credentials, request bodies and transferred files.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

PHAR OpenSSL signature bypass via algorithm downgrade.

The Phar extension selects the signature verification method from the signature type stored in the archive, and only the OpenSSL types consult the separate .pubkey file holding the trusted public key. An attacker who can modify an OpenSSL-signed Phar archive, but not its public key file, can switch the signature type to a keyless hash such as SHA-256 with a recomputed digest, so the altered archive passes verification even with phar.require_hash enabled. An application that loads the archive may then execute attacker-controlled PHP code. Native, tar-based and zip-based phars are affected.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

Use-after-free via repopulation of last_fatal_error_backtrace global after shutdown.

A fatal error raised while modified INI settings are restored during request shutdown can repopulate the stored fatal error backtrace after the executor has been cleaned up. The request memory is then freed, and a diagnostic emitted before executor initialization in a later request handled by the same PHP-FPM or mod_php worker can access the stale backtrace. The shutdown error requires per-path configuration of max_memory_limit, or of zlib.output_compression together with output_handler (which .user.ini can also set). The early diagnostic requires Apache per-directory configuration or, for PHP-FPM, a PHP_VALUE or PHP_ADMIN_VALUE parameter sent by the front end. This can cause memory corruption and worker crashes, and may allow remote code execution.

This issue affects PHP versions 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. PHP-FPM request smuggling through an unread HTTP request body.

PHP does not discard the unread part of an HTTP request body at request shutdown when the application has opened php://input without reading it to the end. When the front end reuses backend connections, which is not the default in nginx or Apache (for example nginx with fastcgi_keep_conn on, or Apache mod_proxy_fcgi with enablereuse=on), PHP-FPM can parse the leftover bytes as a new FastCGI request. An unauthenticated remote attacker can use a single crafted multipart/form-data request to forge a backend request with chosen parameters such as SCRIPT_FILENAME, REMOTE_ADDR and PHP_ADMIN_VALUE, which can lead to execution of attacker-controlled PHP code. With LSAPI, subsequent requests on the connection can be disrupted.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

PHP-FPM epoll use-after-free can lead to local privilege escalation.

When catch_workers_output is enabled and the epoll event backend is used, the PHP-FPM master can close a worker's output pipe in fpm_child_close() without removing the associated event, and the delayed cleanup can free the worker record while its epoll registration is still active. A later event is then dispatched through a pointer into freed memory. A local attacker who can execute PHP code in an FPM worker can crash the master or execute code with its privileges, commonly root. catch_workers_output is disabled by default but enabled in the official PHP-FPM Docker images.

This issue affects PHP versions from 8.1.20 through 8.1.34, from 8.2.7 before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

PHP-FPM status endpoint XSS via unescaped user and script fields.

The PHP-FPM full status output includes the request method, authentication user and script filename of each worker without escaping them for the HTML, XML or JSON format. When the status endpoint is enabled, an unauthenticated remote attacker can store markup in a worker's scoreboard entry with an ordinary request, for example through the username of an HTTP Basic authentication header that the web server forwards to PHP-FPM, or through the script filename where the attacker can influence it. When a user views the full status page as HTML, the injected JavaScript runs in the origin of that page. The attacker does not need access to the status endpoint. Malformed XML or JSON output can also disrupt monitoring tools.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

The shiro:principal tags in shiro-web (Jakarta Pages) and shiro-jakarta-ee (Jakarta Faces) did not escape their output, which could allow cross-site scripting when a principal value is not fully trusted.
This issue affects all Apache Shiro versions through 3.0.1, only when the principal tag is used.

Mitigation: Upgrade to version 3.0.2 or later, which escapes the output.
Alternatively, validate principal values on input.

The Apaczka.pl WooCommerce plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the '_apaczka[<id>][error_messages] (and sibling subkeys inside _apaczka[])' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.4.8 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. This is exploitable during WooCommerce classic guest checkout because WooCommerce's legacy order storage fires the save_post action with the checkout $_POST still populated, giving unauthenticated attackers a direct write path to order post meta without an authenticated session.

`DefaultPasswordService` and `SimpleCredentialsMatcher` could treat an empty stored credential as a match for an empty submitted password.
This issue affects all Apache Shiro versions through 3.0.1, only when accounts with an empty stored credential exist.

Mitigation: Upgrade to version 3.0.2 or later, which fixes the issue.
Alternatively, avoid storing empty credentials, and reject empty passwords in the application.

When PropertiesRealm reloads its properties file, removed users and narrowed permissions could remain in effect.
This issue affects all Apache Shiro versions through 3.0.1, only when PropertiesRealm`loads its properties from a file, which is reloaded periodically by default.

Mitigation: Upgrade to version 3.0.2 or later, which fixes the issue.
Alternatively, restart the application after removing users or narrowing permissions.

When authentication caching is enabled on DefaultLdapRealm, after a user logs in successfully once, subsequent logins for that user succeed with any password.
A cached authentication skips the LDAP bind, and the AllowAllCredentialsMatcher installed by default in DefaultLdapRealm accepts any credentials, allowing an attacker who knows a valid username to authenticate as that user.
This issue affects all Apache Shiro versions through 3.0.0, only when using DefaultLdapRealm (or JndiLdapRealm) with authenticationCachingEnabled set to true, which is not the default.

Mitigation: Upgrade to version 3.0.1 or later, which fixes the issue by no longer installing AllowAllCredentialsMatcher by default.
Alternatively, disable authentication caching on the LDAP realm (this is the default), or configure a credentials matcher, such as SimpleCredentialsMatcher, that verifies credentials against the cached authentication info.
