In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), the pem_agent role, which every PEM agent login inherits, is a member of the PostgreSQL pg_read_server_files and pg_write_server_files roles on the PEM backend database. An attacker who controls any monitored host, and so its PEM agent certificate, can read and write files on the PEM server host as the postgres operating system user. This includes the PEM certificate authority key, which lets the attacker issue certificates for other agents and act as them.
From PEM 10.6.1, PEM agents no longer hold these roles.

In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), the row-level security policies on pem.job and pem.jobstep that apply to PEM agents do not limit an agent to its own jobs. An attacker who controls one monitored host, and so its PEM agent certificate, can create, change or delete jobs for every other agent, including the agent on the PEM server. Agents run SQL job steps with the database credentials of the server they monitor, and shell job steps where batch jobs are enabled, so compromising one monitored host can give superuser SQL access to every monitored database and to the PEM backend.
From PEM 10.6.1, PEM agents can no longer create jobs or change job definitions or job steps.

In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), several SECURITY DEFINER functions in the pem schema of the PEM backend database are owned by a superuser but do not set a safe search_path. Any PEM user who can connect to the PEM backend database can create objects that these functions use in place of the intended ones, and so run arbitrary SQL with superuser privileges. Temporary objects can be used for this on every supported PostgreSQL version, and objects in the public schema on PostgreSQL 14 backends and backends upgraded from PostgreSQL 14.
From PEM 10.6.1, these functions run with a fixed search_path.

In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), multi-factor authentication (MFA) is not enforced on the PEM web application's own routes. An attacker who knows the password of a user who has enrolled a second factor can skip the second factor and call PEM's pages and APIs directly, with that user's permissions. A similar issue in pgAdmin 4 was assigned CVE-2024-4215.
From PEM 10.6.1, every authenticated PEM route requires a completed MFA check.

In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), the SQL Profiler save and load functions in the PEM web application do not keep the client-supplied file name inside the user's storage directory. A user with the SQL Profiler role (pem_comp_sqlprofiler) can read JSON files, and overwrite files that the PEM web server account can write, outside their own storage directory. Overwriting the PEM web application's configuration database stops the web console for all users.
From PEM 10.6.1, the SQL Profiler only reads and writes files inside the user's storage directory.

In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), webhook URLs are not validated, and the PEM agent does not restrict the URL schemes it uses to deliver webhooks. A user with the alert configuration role (pem_config_alert) can set up a webhook with a file:// URL. When the webhook is sent, the agent on the PEM server, which runs as root by default, reads the local file and stores its contents in the webhook error record in the PEM database, where any PEM user can read it.
From PEM 10.6.1, PEM accepts and sends only http and https webhook URLs.

In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), any PEM user can read the encrypted passwords that PEM agents use to connect to monitored servers, including the PEM backend superuser password stored when the PEM server is configured. Unless a custom encryption key is configured, these passwords are encrypted with a key that is the same in every PEM installation, so they can be decrypted.
From PEM 10.6.1, PEM users can no longer read these passwords.

In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), the pem.deploy_job_template() function does not check that the caller can access the servers, groups and agents it deploys a job template to. When PEM teams are used to separate access, a user with the scheduled tasks role (pem_manage_schedule_task) can deploy and schedule SQL or shell job steps on agents that belong to other teams.
From PEM 10.6.1, PEM checks team access for every server, group and agent a template is deployed to.

In Postgres Enterprise Manager (PEM), any PEM user can run the pem.send_webhook() function, which runs with elevated privileges and queues a payload for any configured webhook. The PEM agent then delivers it with that webhook's stored headers, OAuth token or client certificate, so a user can send forged notifications to endpoints they could not otherwise authenticate to.
From PEM 10.6.1, no PEM login role can call this function directly. PEM still sends webhook notifications through its own internal paths.

Vtiger CRM through 8.4.0 contains a blind SQL injection vulnerability that allows authenticated non-administrative users to inject SQL through the k (does not contain) comparator in list view search_params. Attackers can send crafted search_params to the ListAjax getRecordsCount mode, breaking out of the unescaped NOT LIKE clause to extract database contents via boolean or time-based techniques.

Vtiger CRM through 8.4.0 contains a blind SQL injection vulnerability that allows authenticated low-privileged users to inject SQL via unescaped clientid values in the wsapp_map webservice operation. Attackers can register a sync application with wsapp_register, then send delete-mode entries with quoted clientid values processed by SyncServer.php to extract database contents including administrator access keys.

Vtiger CRM through 8.4.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability that allows authenticated users with export access to inject SQL through unvalidated selected_ids values in ExportData.php. Attackers can send a UNION SELECT payload in selected_ids[] to the ExportSelectedRecords mode and read password hashes and access keys from the exported CSV.

Vtiger CRM through 8.4.0 contains a PHP code injection vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to inject code via the updatedFields parameter into config.inc.php. Attackers can supply a crafted HELPDESK_SUPPORT_EMAIL_ID value that passes email validation but closes the PHP string literal to execute arbitrary operating system commands.

Vtiger CRM through 8.4.0 contains a blind SQL injection vulnerability in ReportRun::generateAdvFilterSql() that allows authenticated low-privileged users to inject SQL via the bw comparator. Attackers can send a crafted advanced_filter parameter containing a single quote to the Reports getRecordsCount action to break out of BETWEEN literals and extract database contents.

MP4v2 through 2.1.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in MP4RtpHintTrack::GetPayload() in src/rtphint.cpp that passes an unchecked rtpmap value to strchr(). Attackers can supply a crafted MP4 file whose RTP hint track has a corrupted hinf atom to crash mp4info or applications calling MP4GetHintTrackRtpPayload().

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in DoWriteMeta() in src/isomedia/isom_store.c that allows attackers to crash MP4Box via crafted files. Attackers can supply an ISOBMFF file with a meta box containing an iloc entry but no dref box, crashing MP4Box during rewrite operations like -unhint.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in gf_node_try_destroy that allows attackers to crash MP4Box by supplying crafted XMT scene files. Commands created inside a PROTO scope keep a raw pointer to a freed prototype sub-scene graph, which is read during teardown, causing denial of service.

GPAC MP4Box through 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in gf_node_try_destroy because Conditional node commands keep raw pointers to target nodes freed by gf_sg_reset(). Attackers can supply a crafted XMT scene processed with -info or -add to trigger heap use-after-free, crashing the process and corrupting heap memory.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a type confusion vulnerability in xmt_parse_script_field() that allows attackers to trigger a heap out-of-bounds read via duplicate Script field names with conflicting types. Attackers can craft an XMT file that, when imported with MP4Box, causes gf_sg_vrml_mf_reset() to treat a single-value field as multi-value, crashing the application.

Attendize through 2.8.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in EventOrdersController::postCancelOrder() that allows authenticated organisers to cancel attendees belonging to other accounts' events. Attackers can cancel one of their own orders while supplying foreign attendee IDs, which Attendee::findFromSelection() loads unfiltered, invalidating tickets for any event on the installation.

GPAC MP4Box before 26.07.0 contains a use-after-free vulnerability in Conditional_execute() because SetupConditional() stores a BIFS decoder pointer that gf_sm_load_run_isom() later frees without clearing. Attackers can supply a crafted MP4 file with a BIFS Conditional node processed with -nstatx to crash MP4Box and potentially corrupt the heap.

A flaw was found in Moodle. The grade feedback web service does not properly verify group and course enrolment permissions. An authenticated user with non-editing teacher privileges can exploit this vulnerability to access grade feedback and user profile details across groups or courses they are not authorized to view, leading to unauthorized information disclosure.

A flaw was found in Moodle's Blackboard question import format. Insufficient validation of file paths during the question import process allows an authenticated user with permissions to import questions into a question bank to read arbitrary files accessible to the web server process. An attacker could leverage this vulnerability to view sensitive files, resulting in unauthorized information disclosure.

A flaw was found in Moodle. Due to a missing capability check in the grade items web service, an authenticated user with a student role can view the names of all grade items in a course, including those intended to be hidden. This flaw leads to unauthorized information disclosure of hidden course assessment details.

A flaw was found in Moodle's external database enrolment plugin. Insufficient sanitization of data passed to queries against the external database allows an authenticated user with course editing permissions to perform a Structured Query Language (SQL) injection attack. When this non-default plugin is enabled, an attacker can exploit this issue to view, modify, or delete sensitive records within the connected external database.

A flaw was found in Moodle. Due to insufficient validation when saving activity settings, an authenticated user with teacher privileges can modify activities in courses they are not authorized to access. This flaw allows unauthorized changes to course materials, compromising the integrity of course content.

A flaw was found in Moodle. Insufficient sanitization of objective identifiers in the SCORM (Sharable Content Object Reference Model) objectives report allows an authenticated user with content upload permissions to inject malicious scripts. When another user views the report, the injected script executes in their browser session, potentially allowing the attacker to access sensitive information or perform unauthorized actions on their behalf.

A flaw was found in Moodle. Due to insufficient permission checks and input validation in the quiz question bank callback, an authenticated user can access and view questions from question banks they do not have permission to access. Furthermore, this issue allows users to trigger arbitrary class instantiation (creating unintended application objects), potentially leading to further unauthorized actions.

A flaw was found in Moodle. Missing ownership verification in Feedback activity templates allows an authenticated teacher to view, use, or delete templates associated with courses other than their own. This can result in unauthorized access, modification, or deletion of course materials.

A flaw was found in Moodle. Due to missing ownership checks in badge alignments, an authenticated user with badge management privileges can view and modify alignments associated with badges they do not own. This vulnerability can lead to unauthorized data disclosure and tampering with badge configurations.

A flaw was found in Moodle. An improper authorization check when displaying individual glossary entries allows an authenticated user to view approved glossary items from courses they do not have permission to access. This vulnerability leads to unauthorized information disclosure of restricted educational materials.

A flaw was found in Moodle. Missing authorization checks in the forum discussion web services allow authenticated users to view discussion information in courses they do not have permission to access. In addition, users with teacher privileges may lock forum discussions in courses where they lack proper authorization. This issue can lead to unauthorized information disclosure and unauthorized discussion state modification.

A flaw was found in Moodle. Due to a missing authorization check when viewing and restoring wiki page versions, an authenticated user can access content from courses they are not permitted to view. This issue allows an attacker to inspect restricted course material and copy it into their own wiki pages, leading to unauthorized information disclosure.

A flaw was found in Moodle. Due to a missing authorization check when editing Lesson activity pages, authenticated users with teacher privileges can view and move lesson pages from courses they are not permitted to access into their own lessons. This issue can lead to unauthorized access and modification of restricted course content.

A flaw was found in Moodle. Insufficient authorization checks in the quiz editing functionality allow an authenticated user with teacher privileges to view slot details and modify sections of quizzes they do not have permission to manage. An attacker could exploit this flaw to alter quiz configurations or disclose quiz structure information without proper authorization.

A flaw was found in Moodle's single view grade report web service. A missing authorization check allows authenticated students to view the names of all grade items in a course, including those configured to be hidden. This vulnerability leads to unauthorized information disclosure.

A flaw was found in Moodle. Insufficient authorization checks in the quiz overrides web service allow an authenticated user with teacher privileges to modify user and group overrides for quizzes they do not have permission to manage. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to improperly alter exam access, deadlines, or testing conditions across unauthorized courses.

A flaw was found in Moodle. Due to insufficient authorization checks in the quiz random question filter web service, an authenticated user with teacher privileges can modify random question settings in quizzes they do not have permission to manage. This flaw allows unauthorized users to alter assessment configurations across courses they do not oversee.

@fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP and WebSocket traffic to an upstream server. In versions from 7.1.0 up to but not including 11.6.10, when the plugin is registered with websocket support enabled, it opens the upstream WebSocket connection with a header set built by the default header rewriter, which forwards the client cookie but never sets the upstream origin option, so the browser origin header is dropped while the authenticating cookie is forwarded. Many WebSocket servers defend against cross-site hijacking by checking the origin and treat a missing origin as a trusted non-browser client, so behind the proxy that check never sees the foreign origin. A malicious page visited by a logged-in user can therefore open a WebSocket through the proxy to an upstream that authenticates the handshake with a cookie, and read or send messages on the user's behalf. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.10, and users should upgrade to 11.6.10 or later. As a workaround, provide a header rewriter that sets a correct origin, or validate the origin before the proxy.

Gogs through 0.14.4 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows collaborators with write access to push to protected branches by merging pull requests. Because MergePullRequest skips branch protection checks and PullRequest.Merge omits hook environment variables, attackers can merge commits into branches restricted to allowlisted users.

OFFIS DCMTK 3.5.4 through 3.7.1 contains an integer overflow in DJCodecEncoder::encodeTrueLossless size checks that allows attackers to trigger a heap out-of-bounds read. Attackers can supply a crafted DICOM file with large Columns, Rows and SamplesPerPixel values that, when compressed with true-lossless JPEG, crashes the application.

modified eCommerce Shopsoftware through 3.3.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to inject scripts via the unsanitized products_model field. Attackers with product editing permission can store JavaScript that executes in browsers of other administrators, storefront visitors, and customers viewing carts and order history.

Tiptap @tiptap/core 3.7.0 before 3.30.5 contains a regular expression denial of service vulnerability in parseAttributes and parseShortcodeAttributes that allows attackers to exhaust CPU through quadratic backtracking. Attackers can supply Markdown with long crafted attribute strings parsed by createBlockMarkdownSpec, createAtomBlockMarkdownSpec or createInlineMarkdownSpec to stall browser pages or server processes.

WatchAlert 2.0.0 through 3.9.20 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in the /api/w8t/datasource/dataSourceGet endpoint that lets authenticated users read other tenants' datasources because lookups omit tenant_id filtering. Tenant members with datasource view permission can request another tenant's datasource ID to obtain basic auth passwords, AWS and Alibaba Cloud keys, and Kubernetes kubeconfigs.

MISP contains an authorization and input-validation flaw in its event push mechanism. When a user with push permissions initiates a push of events to a remote MISP instance, the system fails to enforce two critical checks: (1) it does not verify that an event is published before including it in the push, allowing unpublished (i.e., not yet publicly shared) events to be transmitted to the remote server; and (2) it does not verify that the pushing user has read access to the event, causing events the user cannot fetch to be sent as empty event shells, thereby disclosing the existence and metadata of events the user is not authorized to view. Additionally, the remote server's reply selecting which offered events to accept is used without validating that the selected identifiers actually correspond to events in the offered set, potentially allowing the remote to reference events outside the intended scope. The vulnerability requires an authenticated user with push permissions on the source MISP instance and a configured push target. The security impact is unauthorized disclosure of confidential threat-intelligence data (unpublished events and events restricted by user permissions) to a remote MISP instance that should not receive them.

Goproxy before 1.9.4 contains a weak key generation vulnerability in NewCounterEncryptorRandFromKey that derives RSA and Ed25519 leaf certificate private keys from public data due to misuse of hash.Sum. Attackers with the CA certificate and one observed leaf certificate can regenerate that host's leaf private key and impersonate the host to clients trusting the proxy CA.

MISP contains a vulnerability in the cryptographic signature verification of protected events. When a MISP instance signs a protected event for synchronization, it strips all whitespace from the JSON body before computing the PGP signature (preg_replace("/\s+/", "", $data)). The receiving instance performs the same whitespace-stripping before verification. Because the signature covers only the whitespace-free representation, a network relay positioned between two MISP instances can insert whitespace characters into JSON object keys (effectively renaming fields) or into identifier values such as UUIDs, timestamps, and distribution fields without invalidating the signature. The receiving instance accepts the modified event as authentic.

The vulnerability affects the protected event synchronization path: event creation (EventsController::add), event editing (EventsController::edit), event viewing (EventsController::view1), and server-to-server pull synchronization (ServerSyncTool, Server model). An attacker with a network position to intercept and modify traffic between MISP instances can alter the semantic content of protected events while the PGP signature still validates, undermining the integrity guarantees that protected events are designed to provide.

The fix introduces two complementary mechanisms. First, a post-verification scan rejects any received body that contains whitespace in JSON keys (except under Galaxy cluster 'meta' keys) or in identifier-like values (uuid, id, timestamp, distribution, date). Second, a new exact-byte signature scheme (x-pgp-signature-v2) signs the body as transmitted, without whitespace normalization. MISP 3.0 and later peers exchange this exact-byte signature; older peers retain the legacy whitespace-stripped signature. A signature_version field is embedded in protected events so that a 3.0 receiver refuses a body carrying that marker if only the legacy signature is present. Both mechanisms together close the whitespace-injection vector while preserving backward compatibility with pre-3.0 instances.

Incorrect privilege assignment in the user and group reconciliation logic in AWS ssosync before 2.9.5 might allow an authenticated remote user who is assigned a reused Google Workspace e-mail address or group name to inherit the IAM Identity Center group memberships and permission set assignments of a previously synchronized, unrelated identity, via automatic synchronization of that Google Workspace account or group.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to version 2.9.5 or later.

A flaw was found in quarkus-vertx-utils. When a client disconnects while receiving a streaming response, the server fails to detect the closed connection and continues processing the data indefinitely. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit this issue by repeatedly initiating streaming requests and disconnecting, exhausting worker threads and resulting in a Denial of Service (DoS).

A vulnerability was determined in smartalock wireguard-lwip up to cfba91666590e86bd67842c71cedf9a423be823a. Impacted is the function mul of the file src/crypto/refc/x25519.c of the component X25519 Ladder. Executing a manipulation can lead to out-of-bounds write. The attack can be executed remotely. This product implements a rolling release for ongoing delivery, which means version information for affected or updated releases is unavailable. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

A weakness has been identified in OSGeo shapelib up to 1.6.3. This vulnerability affects the function DBFCloneEmpty of the file dbfopen.c. This manipulation causes null pointer dereference. It is possible to launch the attack on the local host. Patch name: f79050a900d2a05529501b2b714b8f89067db071. It is recommended to apply a patch to fix this issue.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. When an administrator revokes tokens by setting a not-before revocation cutoff, Keycloak fails to enforce this boundary when processing User-Managed Access (UMA) grant requests using ID token claims. An authenticated remote user with an active session can submit a previously revoked ID token to receive a fresh Requesting Party Token (RPT). This flaw allows an attacker to bypass token revocation and retain unauthorized access to protected resources.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. When processing token requests using the User-Managed Access (UMA) grant, Keycloak fails to verify whether a target client or resource server is enabled before issuing an authorization token. An authenticated remote user can exploit this flaw to obtain valid Requesting Party Tokens (RPTs) for disabled clients, bypassing administrative access controls and permissions restrictions.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. The Account API endpoint for sharing resources fails to verify whether owner-managed access is enabled and accepts permission scopes not assigned to the resource. An authenticated user can exploit this vulnerability to generate pre-granted permission tickets, causing Keycloak to bypass policy evaluation and issue access tokens with unauthorized scopes.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. When a client application enforces step-up authentication or multi-factor authentication (MFA) via a minimum authentication level, Keycloak fails to apply this requirement to login sessions initiated through the credential reset endpoint. An attacker who possesses a user's initial credentials (such as a password) can navigate from the reset interface back to the standard login form and authenticate without completing the required second factor. This flaw allows an attacker to obtain valid access tokens and gain unauthorized access to protected services without satisfying mandatory security controls.

Quasar before 2.35.3 contains a DOM clobbering vulnerability that allows attackers to break native wrapper detection by injecting HTML elements named Capacitor, cordova, or StatusBar. Attackers can place markup such as a div with id Capacitor into server-rendered or pre-rendered HTML so app.use(Quasar) throws and the application never mounts, or openURL() and AddressbarColor.set() throw.

Stoatchat before 0.16.5 contains an unbounded JXL image decoding vulnerability in revolt_files decode_image that allows unauthenticated attackers to exhaust memory via the january /proxy endpoint. Attackers can request a small hosted JXL file declaring 12000x12000 pixels through /proxy to trigger huge allocations, OOM-killing january and denying proxy and embed service.

Tandoor Recipes before 2.7.4 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows space admins to reach internal hosts because Nextcloud.get_client builds WebDAV clients from Storage.url without calling safe_request. Attackers can create a NEXTCLOUD storage via POST /api/storage/ pointing at internal hosts, import a file, then call GET /api/get_recipe_file/<id>/ to read internal service or cloud metadata responses.

Manyfold 0.124.0 before 0.154.2 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to make the instance fetch internal URLs by supplying malicious ActivityPub actor icon.url and image.url fields. Attackers can deliver Create or Update activities to the inbox, causing the Shrine remote_url plugin to request internal or cloud metadata hosts and store responses as creator avatar or banner attachments.

SABnzbd before 5.2.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the Sorter that allows attackers to write files outside the Complete folder via crafted propername, episodename or job name (%dn) values. Attackers can supply a malicious NZB with '...' sequences that collapse to '..' after single-pass replacement, moving downloaded files into arbitrary directories writable by SABnzbd.

OpnForm before 2.8.2 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to move other forms' shared assets by supplying their URLs in file upload fields. Attackers can submit a public form with another form's cover or logo URL, causing Storage::move() to relocate it into submissions and break that asset.

diaspora* before 0.10.0 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject iframe attributes via the maxheight parameter of the GET /oembed endpoint. Attackers can supply a single quote in maxheight to inject an onload handler into the returned html, executing script in third-party oEmbed consumers that embed it unsanitized.

diaspora* before 0.10.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users to inject script by crafting og:video:secure_url values. Attackers can post links to pages whose allowlisted-prefix video URL contains a quote and onload handler, executing script in readers' sessions when they click the video preview.

node-soap before 1.14.1 contains a prototype pollution vulnerability in WSDL.xmlToObject that allows unauthenticated attackers to pollute Object.prototype via an XML element with id="__proto__". Attackers can send a single crafted SOAP request to a soap.listen() server, or return a malicious response to a client, causing all subsequent SOAP parsing to fail until process restart.

parse5 7.0.0 before 8.1.1 contains an uncaught exception vulnerability in Preprocessor#_processSurrogate that allows remote attackers to crash applications by supplying two consecutive low surrogates. Attackers can submit input such as U+DC00 U+DC00, which decodes to out-of-range code point 0x110000 and throws a RangeError from parse, parseFragment, or streaming parsers, crashing Node.js processes.

modified eCommerce Shopsoftware through 3.3.0 contains a local file inclusion vulnerability that allows administrators to include arbitrary server files by storing ../ sequences in the content manager file name. Unauthenticated requests to shop_content.php then pass the stored path to include(), executing embedded PHP in uploaded content files or images as the web server user.

modified eCommerce Shopsoftware through 3.3.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in admin/support.php that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject script via the module parameter. Attackers can trick a logged-in administrator into opening a crafted link to run script in the admin panel, reading CSRF tokens and changing shop settings.

THC-Hydra through 9.7 contains a stack buffer overflow vulnerability in analyze_server_response() of hydra-http-form.c that allows malicious HTTP servers to corrupt memory via crafted Set-Cookie headers. Attackers can send a Set-Cookie header with an extra leading space followed by a repeated cookie name, causing a negative strncpy length that overflows tmpcookie and crashes Hydra.

A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) could allow an unauthenticated attacker to conduct an arbitrary file upload attack due to insufficient file type validation. A successful exploit could allow an attacker to upload arbitrary files to the target system. This is MTLVULN-1861.

When extra data is allowed (extra=Extra.allow), providing a __pydantic_initialised__ key when validating a Pydantic V1 dataclass makes it considered as already validated, resulting in field values not being validated. The __init__() method of Pydantic V1 dataclasses stores all the provided keyword arguments in the instance __dict__ before validation, so a __pydantic_initialised__ keyword argument overrides the internal flag used to skip validation of already validated instances. As a result, data returned by validation doesn't match the declared type. Affected are applications validating untrusted data into Pydantic V1 dataclasses allowing extra data. The issue was fixed in Pydantic 1.10.27. Users relying on the pydantic.v1 namespace in Pydantic V2 should upgrade to 2.14.2 or later.

sqlmap before 1.10.11.89 contains a credential exposure vulnerability that allows attackers to capture user-supplied Cookie and Authorization headers by redirecting requests to another host. Attackers controlling the scanned target or abusing an open redirect can make RedirectHandler.http_error_302 forward session cookies or bearer tokens to an attacker-controlled host.

VideoLAN libaacs 0.7.0 through 0.12.0 on non-macOS, non-Windows builds contains stack-based buffer overflows in aacs_resolve_path() in src/file/path.c from length checks against the wrong buffer. Local attackers can place a symlink with a long target on a disc path a user opens to overflow resolved_path[] and link[], crashing the process or potentially executing code if mitigations are bypassed.

ClassiCube before 1.4.0 contains a heap-based out-of-bounds write vulnerability in Png_Reconstruct in src/Bitmap.c that occurs when AVERAGE and PAETH filters process zero-width PNG images. A malicious multiplayer server can supply a crafted texture pack URL or player skin to write past the heap buffer, corrupting memory and crashing connecting clients.

@scalar/typebox before 0.1.4 contains a code injection vulnerability in TypeCompiler that allows attackers to execute JavaScript by supplying crafted schema strings. Attackers can inject single-quote breakouts into string format, Kind names, property keys or Literal values to run arbitrary JavaScript in the host Node.js process during Compile() and Check().

Wing FTP Server before 8.2.8 contains a file mask bypass vulnerability allowing attackers to upload restricted files via an embedded NUL byte in Upload Link filenames. Attackers can plant a Lua session file with a chosen UID and send a matching UID cookie to execute operating system commands as the service account.

A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) could allow an unauthenticated attacker to conduct an authentication bypass attack due to improper handling of authentication. The UiChemy – Convert Figma, Prompts and AI Builds to Elementor, Gutenberg and Bricks plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'sections[0][settings][raw_css]' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.5.3 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with contributor-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The sanitizer bypass relies on HTML entity-encoding the CSS breakout payload at save time, which passes the byte-based filter unchanged and is later reconstituted into executable markup by the render-time html_entity_decode call.

Validating an untrusted ISO 8601 duration string into a timedelta field with Pydantic V1 takes quadratic time: an input of a few dozen kilobytes takes seconds to validate.

The iso8601_duration_re regular expression used to parse ISO 8601 durations (in pydantic/datetime_parse.py) contains an unescaped ".", which also matches digits. On a string of digits, the repeated groups overlap and the regex engine backtracks in quadratic time.

The issue was fixed in commit 62791e66a9f8f118e465ed760c9e2ede9ae3055e. Users relying on the pydantic.v1 namespace in Pydantic V2 should upgrade to 2.14.2 or later.

Impact: denial of service through validation of untrusted input. Affected are applications validating untrusted strings into timedelta fields.

Validating an untrusted list into a field constrained with unique_items=True with Pydantic V1 takes quadratic time: an input of a few hundred kilobytes takes seconds to validate.

The ConstrainedList.unique_items_validator validator (in pydantic/types.py) checks each item against all the following ones. For a list with no duplicates (the common, valid case), this results in a quadratic number of comparisons.

The issue was fixed in commit 6ec75e57f277a820ec583e601167f25fe8dc7c87. Users relying on the pydantic.v1 namespace in Pydantic V2 should upgrade to 2.14.2 or later.

Impact: denial of service through validation of untrusted input. Affected are applications validating untrusted lists into fields constrained with unique_items=True (using conlist() or Field()).

The fix only applies to lists of builtin scalar types (int, float, str, bytes, bool and None), for which duplicates can be detected in linear time. Lists of other types (e.g. models or dictionaries) are still checked in quadratic time, as their items aren't guaranteed to be hashable: bound their size using the max_items constraint.

Pydantic V2 models are not affected.

When extra data is allowed, providing both the alias and the name of an aliased TypedDict or dataclass field makes the unvalidated value (provided under the name) overwrite the validated one (provided under the alias), resulting in validated data not matching the declared type.

Extra items are stored in the same dictionary as the fields (the returned dictionary for TypedDict, the instance __dict__ for dataclasses). As only the alias is marked as used, the field name is treated as an extra item, and its unvalidated value overrides the validated one. The TypedDict validator (pydantic-core/src/validators/typed_dict.rs) and the dataclass validator (pydantic-core/src/validators/dataclass.rs) share this logic.

The issue was fixed in commit 34491f5328f168f14e3769cd5f0f83c0af0f4778.

Impact: validation bypass, as data returned by validation doesn't match the declared type. Affected are applications validating untrusted data into TypedDict or dataclass types with aliased fields and extra data allowed (with extra='allow', or with the extra_items argument for TypedDict), using Pydantic V2 (up to and including 2.14.1).

Pydantic models (BaseModel) are not affected, as extra data is stored separately from fields.

Validating an untrusted string in exponent notation into a Fraction field computes the full power of ten without any bound: an input of a few bytes takes seconds to validate.

String inputs are passed to the Fraction constructor. For strings in exponent notation (e.g. '1e8000000'), CPython computes the corresponding power of ten as an integer (in Lib/fractions.py).

The issue was fixed in commit 69ed168e9ad465eef4c8d81efb152a93b604daf5. For strings in exponent notation, the exponent is now parsed before calling the Fraction constructor, and exponents larger than 4300 (in absolute value) are rejected.

Impact: denial of service through validation of untrusted input. Affected are applications validating untrusted strings into Fraction fields (in both JSON and Python mode, including in strict mode), using Pydantic from 2.10.0 up to (but excluding) 2.14.0.

From 2.14.0, exponents larger than 4300 (in absolute value) are rejected, matching the maximum number of digits accepted for integers.

Validating an untrusted URL with a long scheme and many hosts into a multi-host URL field (e.g. PostgresDsn) takes quadratic time and memory: an input of about a hundred kilobytes takes around a gigabyte of memory to validate.

The parse_multihost_url() function (in pydantic-core/src/validators/url.rs) parses each host separately, prepending the whole URL prefix (including the scheme) to every one of them. As the scheme can be arbitrarily long, and is parsed and stored once per host, both time and memory grow quadratically with the input size. Allowed schemes (e.g. postgres for PostgresDsn) are only checked after parsing, so they don't prevent the issue.

The issue was fixed in commit b4028f9d87e34750e53be0ba011d70f3c0fcc94e.

Impact: denial of service through validation of untrusted input. Affected are applications validating untrusted strings into multi-host URL fields (PostgresDsn, MongoDsn, NatsDsn, or custom types built on MultiHostUrl).

When validating JSON data into a model allowing extra data, the keys of extra data aren't validated against the key type annotated on __pydantic_extra__, resulting in extra data not matching the declared type. This is the case if you define __pydantic_extra__ as e.g. dict[Annotated[str, Field(pattern=r'^x_')], int].

The validate_json_by_iteration() method (in pydantic-core/src/validators/model_fields.rs), used to validate JSON data into models, only validates the values of extra data, and stores the keys as is.

The issue was fixed in commit 4c65dbda9970a488e2ff21c8693fc6f6d70a3358.

Impact: validation bypass, as extra data returned by validation doesn't match the declared type. Affected are applications validating untrusted JSON data into models allowing extra data (with extra='allow'), with a key type annotated on __pydantic_extra__ (e.g. dict[Annotated[str, Field(pattern=...)], int]), using Pydantic from 2.13.0 up to (but excluding) 2.14.2.

Python mode validation isn't affected.

A flaw was found in Keycloak. This vulnerability allows an authenticated remote attacker to cause a denial of service by terminating active sessions of arbitrary users. When processing Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) documents that lack a root signature, Keycloak accepts the request as long as any assertion within the document is signed, without verifying its context or placement. An attacker holding a validly signed assertion can embed it into an unsigned logout request for another user, causing Keycloak to accept the forged request and terminate the victim's session.

In Dolibarr before 24.0.3, dolForgeSQLCriteriaCallback() in htdocs/core/lib/functions.lib.php allows account takeover because it strips only a single table-name prefix from a Universal Search Filter (sqlfilters) operand before checking it against the forbidden-field denylist (pass, pass_crypted, api_key). MariaDB and MySQL accept a two-level qualification such as schema.alias.column, so an operand of the form dolibarr.u.pass_crypted survives the check and is emitted into the WHERE clause. A remote authenticated user holding only the holiday read and readall permissions, which confer no user-management or administrative access, can use the resulting boolean oracle at GET /api/index.php/holidays to recover any user's bcrypt password hash and api_key one character at a time, including an administrator's. Because api_key is accepted directly by the REST API as a bearer credential, this yields full administrative control of the application. This bypasses the fix for CVE-2026-89012, which added only a strtolower() call and did not address prefix depth. The same denylist also omits pass_temp, which stores a password in cleartext, as well as national_registration_number, salary, birth, address, personal_mobile and note_private.

When message history is serialized and loaded again, a tool result that contains a JSON object in the serialized shape of one of Pydantic AI's file types is rebuilt as that file. A third party who controls data a tool returns, such as a record that an MCP server or a function tool returns from an external system, can use this to make the application download a URL on its local network, or make the model provider read an s3:// object or uploaded file with the application's credentials. Applications are affected when tool results can contain third-party data, message history containing those results is serialized and loaded again (stored history, history a UI adapter holds on the server, or Temporal, DBOS or Prefect durable execution), and the model is one Pydantic AI downloads files for, one that honors force_download, or one whose provider resolves non-HTTP file URLs or uploaded files. History that a client submits through the Vercel AI or AG-UI adapter in the default mode is not affected. The issue is fixed in pydantic-ai and pydantic-ai-slim 1.107.10 and 2.66.0.

Dokploy 0.28.0 before 0.31.1 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the patch.readRepoDirectories tRPC procedure that allows authenticated organization members to list tracked files of arbitrary git repositories. Bar Assistant 3.0.0 before 6.11.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in BarController::join that allows authenticated users to join bars without a valid invite code. BeamNG.drive before 0.40.6 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability because JIT-compiled LuaJIT traces omit FFI array bounds checks, letting untrusted Lua escape the sandbox. Attackers supplying a malicious mod can JIT-compile an FFI store loop, write out of range using a tostring() address leak, re-enable ffi.load, and run commands as the game user.
